The Gulf Coast is on alert as Tropical Storm Bertha churns toward populated areas, threatening flooding rain, dangerous storm surge and damaging wind gusts, while Hurricane Fausto has strengthened in the eastern Pacific but poses no immediate threat to land.

Bertha, the second named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season, formed Monday evening and was about 140 miles (225 kilometers) south of Panama City, Florida. The storm had maximum sustained winds of 40 mph (65 kph) and was expected to strengthen as it edges toward the northern Gulf Coast, according to the National Hurricane Center in Miami.

Forecasters warned the slow-moving storm could linger near the coast for days, raising the risk of prolonged heavy rain, flash flooding and coastal inundation from Florida to Louisiana before drifting west toward Texas.

open image in gallery A satellite view of Tropical Storm Bertha forming over the eastern Gulf of Mexico near Florida ( Reuters )

By Monday night, Bertha was nearly stationary but was forecast to turn west or west-northwest over the next several days.

A tropical storm warning is in effect from the Alabama-Florida border west to southeastern Louisiana, while a storm surge watch stretches from the mouth of the Mississippi River to the Alabama-Florida border.

The hurricane center warned that life-threatening storm surge of up to 4 feet (1.2 meters) is possible in parts of Louisiana, Alabama and Florida. Bertha could also spawn isolated tornadoes across Florida's Big Bend.

open image in gallery This satellite image from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration taken at 7:31pm EDT shows Tropical Storm Bertha in the Gulf of Mexico ( AP )

Forecasters said flash flooding is possible through Friday from western Florida to central Texas. Louisiana could see 3 to 5 inches (7 to 12 centimeters) of rain, with isolated areas receiving significantly higher totals.

Communities are already preparing for the storm. Red flags flew along the beach in Orange Beach, Alabama, warning swimmers of dangerous surf and rip currents, while emergency officials in Florida's Escambia County distributed sand to residents filling sandbags in flood-prone neighborhoods.

Farther west, Hurricane Fausto strengthened Monday night about 745 miles (1,200 kilometers) southwest of the southern tip of Mexico's Baja California peninsula.

Fausto had maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (120 kph) and was moving west-northwest at 9 mph (15 kph). No coastal watches or warnings were in effect, but forecasters warned the hurricane could generate dangerous surf and life-threatening rip currents along parts of the Baja California coast.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

News.title: How to have the perfect holiday in France’s gastronomic capital
News.content:
Calling all bon vivants. This is your city. Within seconds of tucking into a traditional andouillette (tripe sausage) or modern vegetarian cuisine in a jam-packed bistro, admiring fine art in a Renaissance abbey, or getting delightfully lost in a traboule (secret passageway) used by 19th-century silk weavers, you’ll quickly realise that Lyon is a city that knows how to live well.

Enthralling, cinematic and richly storied, after living here for 10 years, I still find myself being surprised by a walled garden I never knew, a fresque (wall mural) suddenly popping up on a riverfront wall, a new museum or river boat route.

Street-smart Romans first spotted the city’s extraordinary topography, founding Lugdunum (Lyon’s predecessor) in 43BC on the sunny slopes of Fourvière. And to this day, this basilica-crowned hill above Lyon’s quaint Unesco-listed Old Town (Vieux Lyon) is the perfect perch for clocking the mighty Rhône and Saône rivers that wend their way so gracefully through the centre.

The city’s quays, landscaped with peaceful water gardens and floating bars, buzz night and day – while culture lovers can explore a bounty of museums. Then there’s the gastronomy: among France’s finest, thanks to the unfaltering creativity and sass of city chefs, both past and present.

News.title: The 16 best things to do in Lyon
News.content:
Few dedicated foodies make the pilgrimage to Lyon without dining once chez Paul Bocuse, be it at the late chef’s mythical, out-of-town gastronomic temple in Collonges-au-Mont d’Or (which lost one of its three stars in 2020, having held three since 1965) or at the more affordable Comptoir Paul Bocuse inside landmark covered market Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse. Across the street, admire a larger-than-life portrait of the iconic chef, frescoed onto the side of a building. Inside the market, the moules glacées (cold mussel ‘soup’) at oyster and shellfish specialist Maison Merle and a gooey round of Saint Marcellin cheese from Fromagerie La Mère Richard are other local legends. Avoid buying fruit and veg here unless you have to – weekly outdoor food markets elsewhere in the city are cheaper.

To sample future talent in the Lyonnais kitchen, mingle with students over lunch, dinner or drinks and live music at La Commune – an innovative food court that hosts chefs aspiring to open their own restaurant in Lyon. Resident chefs cook up a storm at La Commune for maximum six months, meaning an ever-changing rollcall of epicurean excitement at this unique culinary incubator.

To extend the experience further afield, consider a road trip along a section of the Vallée de la Gastronomie, stretching 620km (385 miles). In Lyon, the gourmet route delves into the secrets behind chef Joseph Viola’s award-winning duck foie gras and sweetbread pâté en croûte (think French-posh pork pie) and the city’s distinctive offal-based bouchon (Lyonnais bistro) cuisine.

Sports.title: Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez breaks silence on World Cup final heartbreak after red card and riling up England fans
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ insists Argentina players represented their country in “the best possible way” at the World Cup.

The South Americans have faced intense scrutiny for their behaviour during the tournament.



From celebrating with a Falklands flag in the semi-finals to throwing punches after the final – many were glad to see Argentina lose in New Jersey.

Chelsea midfielder Fernandez, 25, has been at the centre of the drama.



He scored a long-range equaliser to help break England hearts last week before being sent off in the final – his first booking being shown for dissent and the second for booting teenager Pau Cubarsi into the air.

But Fernandez insists that he and his team-mates can be proud of how they represented Argentina this summer.



He wrote on Instagram: “As time goes by, you realize there is something much bigger than just the result.

“For years, this group has represented us in the best possible way.

“It teaches that competing isn’t just about winning; it’s about giving your all for the jersey and never giving up.

“It has been a privilege to be part of a group that always stepped up, competed at the highest level, and defended these colors with pride, humility, and commitment.

“Wearing my country’s jersey is the greatest honor of my career, and I will continue to give my all every time I get to defend it.”

Sports.title: Fans baffled as English football icon pops up at the unveiling of new Prime Minister Andy Burnham
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL fans were left baffled after spotting an English football icon at the unveiling of the UK’s new Prime Minister.

Former Mayor of Greater Manchester Andy Burnham was sworn into office at Downing Street on Monday as he replaced Sir Keir Starmer.



However, watchers were stunned to see who one of his loyal followers in the crowd was.

Sporting sunglasses and a white jacket, two-time English title winner Peter Reid was present for Burnham’s unveiling.



Reid, 70, won the Division One title twice with Everton in the 1980s, while also achieving glory with the Toffees by lifting the 1984 FA Cup and 1985 European Cup Winners’ Cup.

The former defensive midfielder was also capped by England 13 times and starred at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico.



Following his playing career, Reid moved into management, which included an exemplary stint as Sunderland boss between 1995 and 2002 as he won the First Division – now the Championship – twice with the Black Cats.

While in the Premier League, he also won the Manager of the Month award twice as he guided a Kevin Phillips-led Sunderland side to competing for a place in European competitions.

Speaking to Sky about his appearance at Burnham’s unveiling, he revealed the four-word message he gave to his fellow Evertonian.

He said: “He’s been a pal of mine for a long time, it was good to see his family there as well. He’s got a job on…



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I just said ‘congratulations, get in there lad’.

“It’s a scouse thing, to the PM as well. I must have forget for a minute.”

Reid added that he heard a message of unity coming from Burnham’s first speech in front of No10.

He also starred for the likes of Bolton, Manchester City and Queens Park Rangers while later enjoying a managerial career encompassing coaching roles as Man City, Leeds, Coventry, Plymouth and Thailand manager.

Sports.title: Newcastle urged to name St James’ Park stand after Kevin Keegan as Toon icon hails legend after his death at 75
Sports.content:
LES FERDINAND has called for Newcastle to pay Kevin Keegan the ultimate tribute by naming a stand after him at St James’ Park.

The Magpies legend passed away at the age of 75 earlier today, following a battle with cancer.



Newcastle icon Alan Shearer and other big names released emotional statements after the gut-wrenching news broke.

Ferdinand took his career to another level when he joined the Toon and notched 43 goals in 69 games under Keegan.



The former striker, 59, reckons Newcastle should rename one of their stands in honour of the two-time Ballon d’Or winner.

He told SunSport: “I really do hope they name one of the St James’ Park stands after Kevin because that would be a fitting tribute.

“What Kevin Keegan did for Newcastle United and the North East region as a whole will never be repeated.

“We will sit here and mourn him but, knowing Kevin, I know that instead he would want everyone to celebrate his life.”

Ferdinand was shocked by Keegan’s character after seeing him enjoy a glittering playing career with the likes of Liverpool and Hamburg.

The St James’ Park favourite added: “He’s the first superstar footballer I know.



“I remember watching him on the TV but when you met him, he was so humble, he was so charismatic.

“And he had a nice habit of just making you feel like a million dollars every time you were around him.

“I know how much he means to the North East and to Newcastle but, further afield, we should be paying him homage for what he’s done for football in general.



“My time with him was as a player at Newcastle so I know full well just how much he did for the region.”

Newcastle came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League title in 1996 and were runners-up again 12 months later.

Ferdinand conceded failing to be crowned champions is among his biggest regrets while on Tyneside.

The ex-Tottenham marksman admitted: “When I swapped QPR for Newcastle, it might have appeared to be a case of leaving the bright lights of London behind.

“But he somehow made the bright lights of Newcastle seem even brighter, if that makes sense. He certainly had a way with words.



“I think he was hell-bent on playing entertaining football and trying to entertain the paying public.

“The boys from that era will all agree we’re so sad we went so close to the top prize but ultimately weren’t able to secure the title for him.

“We enjoyed every minute of playing under him and he made it that way because of the brand of attacking football he wanted us to play.



“He wanted us to enjoy what we were doing and sometimes, as footballers, when you enjoy what you’re doing you’re going to play your best football, which is what we did the majority of the time.

“I think he’ll go down as producing one of the most entertaining teams that the Premier League has ever seen.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Normally people don’t remember who finished as the runners-up over the years, but they certainly remember our near miss.

“I don’t know whether that’s a good thing or a bad thing. But for that period of time, Newcastle were everyone’s second favourite team.”

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal dances wildly and Spain hero trolls Donald Trump as TWO MILLION fans line streets for World Cup bus parade
Sports.content:
LAMINE YAMAL showed off his dance moves on Spain’s open top bus parade while celebrating their World Cup triumph.

Spain returned home to Madrid as heroes this week after beating Argentina 1-0 in Sunday’s final.



The world champions arrived in the Spanish capital in a party mood after adding a second star to their shirt.

Luis de la Fuente’s men wasted little time kicking off the celebrations as they were welcomed back to Spain by a horde of adoring fans.





A total of TWO MILLION supporters lined the streets of Madrid with flags and banners and Barcelona ace Yamal lapped it up.

He enjoyed the scenes as he started dancing with Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams.

The 19-year-old performed a short improvised routine with the winger, who absolutely loved Yamal’s enthusiasm.

Some of his other Spain team-mates were topless while draping themselves in the national team flag and enjoying a few drinks.



And veteran striker Borja Iglesias decided to give himself the role as team DJ as he took to the decks to get the tunes going.

As the incredible atmosphere continued to build, some eagle-eyed fans noticed match-winning hero Ferran Torres was wearing a hilarious cap poking fun at Donald Trump.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The US President had just awarded the team their medals the previous day.

But Torres still took the opportunity to tease him as he wore a red cap that read: “Make Spain Great Again” – mimicking his trademark slogan for America.

Later on the Spain heroes all arrived on stage, with each one being given their own unique entrance music.

New Real Madrid man Marc Cucurella even started playing the drums during his performance.



Spain’s captain Rodri gave a speech to the fans while appearing on stage.

He said: “We’ve won the World Cup. And how many do we have? Two. These guys here are amazing, and I don’t know what else to say.

“I would like to remember a very important person to me, a player who has been unfairly criticized and who today is part of Spanish football history: Ferran.”

Manager De La Fuente added: “Thank you Spain for supporting us, for being here. We are lucky to have 26 fantastic people who are also fantastic footballers, the best in the world.



“For me, it is an honor to manage them and share this moment with my coaching staff. Together we are stronger, don’t forget that. Long live Spain!”

Sports.title: SunSport’s World Cup team of the tournament revealed including England star, wantaway Chelsea ace and veteran hero, 40
Sports.content:
THE World Cup is over with Spain emerging as winners after an incredible tournament.

Several big-name stars have delivered brilliant performances across the last six weeks in North America.



From the usual suspects, to new heroes, plenty of players have catapulted themselves to even greater stardom.

As the tournament winds down, SunSport’s Tom Barclay selects his team of the tournament…



GOALKEEPER: Vozinha, Cape Verde

BECAME an overnight social-media sensation for his stunning shutout against Spain at the start of the tournament.

That splendid display in the 0-0 stalemate against the eventual winners saw his following on Instagram skyrocket from 50,000 pre tournament to 29million.



The 40-year-old free agent also played well against Lionel Messi’s Argentina – surely someone will pick him up this summer?

RIGHT-BACK: Pedro Porro, Spain

THOSE who watched Tottenham scrap to Premier League survival on the final day of the season would not have predicted their two right-backs shining in the World Cup semi-finals.



But while Djed Spence’s heroics were not enough to see England get past Argentina, Porro scored the killer second goal as Spain shocked favourites France.

Porro was sensational all tournament and Spurs will be delighted they managed to tie him down to a bumper five-year contract midway through it.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

CENTRE-BACK: Pau Cubarsi, Spain

AN essential part of a miserly Spanish defence who kept seven clean sheets in eight games.



Playing alongside former Manchester City – and France – centre-back Aymeric Laporte, classy Cubarsi was the model of composure throughout and rightfully won the young player of the tournament award.

Another fantastic product from Barca’s La Masia academy, it is amazing to think he is still only 19.

CENTRE-BACK: Dayot Upamecano, France

DIDIER DESCHAMPS revealed on Friday that Upamecano is known as “the Little Monster” in the France set-up.



Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich team-mate followed up a fine season in the Bundesliga with an impressive tournament.

His speed and technical quality on the ball were key to France conceding only two goals in their first six games, before Luis de la Fuente’s Spain gave Les Bleus the blues.

LEFT-BACK: Marc Cucurella, Spain

CURLY-HAIRED Cucurella has had one heck of a summer.



On the day of Spain’s first game – when they were held to a 0-0 draw by plucky Cape Verde – it was announced the left-back was joining Real Madrid from Chelsea for £50million.

That sparked an excellent World Cup for the ex-Brighton man who was great going forward and a rock in defence as Spain emerged as champions.

DEFENSIVE MIDFIELD: Rodri, Spain

AFTER a season plagued by injury, the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner looked back to his best and took home the player of the tournament award.



Everyone in England knows his terrific ability to grip a game from the base of midfield and he was pivotal in helping Spain follow up their Euro 2024 win with glory here.

How Manchester City must be desperate to get a new contract sorted so they can pair him with £116m new-boy Elliot Anderson.

DEFENSIVE MIDFIELD: Enzo Fernandez, Argentina

THE man we love to hate – or maybe just hate.



But there is no denying the Argentina star is top quality and proved as much with that devastating late equaliser against England in that heartbreaking semi-final.

He massively let himself down in the final with his daft red card but until that point he was key to Argentina getting so close.

ATTACKING MIDFIELD: Michael Olise, France

COPPED a bit of flak for a quiet display against Spain in the semi-final.



But earlier in the tournament Olise was simply sensational, playing in a No10 role and displaying the kind of exquisite, defence-splitting passes that a peak Kevin De Bruyne would be proud of.

Another star Real Madrid have their eyes on this summer, though Bayern Munich team-mate Harry Kane will hope that possible blockbuster switch does not come off.

ATTACKING MIDFIELD: Jude Bellingham, England

WHAT an emphatic answer to anyone doubting him ahead of the tournament.



Kane was very good but Bellingham was unreal in the knockout games against Mexico and Norway, dragging England through with back-to-back braces.

He hit seven goals in total and was the Three Lions’ talisman. Argentina may have shackled him but it does not deny the fact he is a world-class operator who we are lucky to call our own.

STRIKER: Lionel Messi, Argentina

SOME of us had never seen Messi in the flesh until that fateful night in Atlanta – and then left wishing we had not.



The GOAT made a mockery of the fact he is turning 40 next summer by conjuring up two killer late goals to dump out England.

Not only that but he scored a whopping eight goals in the tournament, coming up clutch for the nation that adores him time and again.

STRIKER: Kylian Mbappe, France

MBAPPE wrote on social media that the France team had “failed” outgoing boss Didier Deschamps, who is stepping down after the tournament.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

That is after the tournament favourites were dumped out by Spain in the semis.

But that does not erase another excellent campaign individually by the Real Madrid mega star, whose 10 goals took him to 22 World Cup strikes overall and the golden boot.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero issues statement after World Cup final loss and vile Argentina scenes
Sports.content:
Cristian Romero issues statement after World Cup final loss and vile Argentina scenes

Cristian Romero was unable to win another World Cup with Argentina at the weekend and has opened up on the pain he feels in the wake of the defeat

View 2 Images Cristian Romero cut a dejected figure after Argentina's World Cup final loss (Image: Getty Images)

Cristian Romero has opened up on the "hurt" he feels after Argentina's World Cup defeat but insists "one thing we'll never lack is heart".

‌



The South Americans failed in their bid to win back-to-back World Cups as they were outclassed in Sunday's final by Spain, who scored their winner in extra-time. Argentina had produced some dramatic victories en route to the final but ultimately came up short.

‌



They've copped huge criticism for their physical approach and, most notably, the unsavoury scenes that followed the full-time whistle. Leandro Paredes was sent-off after the final whistle after being pictured shoving Spain’s Eric Garcia by the throat.

‌



Romero made headlines as he went up to collect his runners-up medal, but snubbed a handshake from US President Donald Trump, and the Tottenham defender has issued a heartfelt statement on his social media.

Lionel Messi shows true colours with emotional message after World Cup final loss READ MORE :

Enzo Fernandez breaks silence after World Cup final red card with message to Argentina fans READ MORE :

He said: "And this time, it didn't happen for us. And believe me, it hurts. It hurts a lot, because no one wanted to keep writing this beautiful story more than we did. We dreamed of bringing the cup home again, and it didn't happen.

"But if there's one thing we'll never lack, it's heart. We left it all out there. We had to settle for second place, but we never stopped representing Argentina with the pride and commitment that this jersey deserves. What a pride and fortune it is to be part of this family, damn it @Argentina.

‌



"Sorry we couldn't give you that joy we so wanted to deliver. We play for you, for every Argentine who was cheering from every corner of the world. We feel that love every day.

View 2 Images Argentina were unable to retain their World Cup crown (Image: getty images)

"Today it's time to get back up. Start over. Work harder, believe more, and prepare so that this jersey returns to where we ourselves put it in these last years, at the very top. Because finals aren't handed to you—they're earned by reaching them. And this group, and whoever steps up, will keep fighting, united, with the same dream as always.

‌



"Thank you for being there. Thank you for believing. We'll rise again because that's Argentina. Always together."

Romero will return to Tottenham, who have invested huge sums after securing Premier League survival, but his future with the north Londoners has been questioned over recent months.

Sports.title: Argentina players release telling statements after World Cup final disgrace
Sports.content:
Argentina players release telling statements after World Cup final disgrace

Argentina were beaten by Spain in the World Cup final with FIFA going on to launch an investigation into the players' behaviour after the game

View 4 Images Argentina players watch on after losing to Spain in the World Cup final (Image: Hannah Peters - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Several members of the Argentina squad have issued messages after their defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, with none addressing the chaotic scenes that followed the final whistle. Spain claimed a 1-0 win over Argentina at MetLife Stadium on Sunday night, with Barcelona star Ferran Torres scoring the winning goal in extra time.

‌



However, the final whistle saw a heated exchange between Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes and members of the Spain squad.

‌



Paredes appeared to kick Eric Garcia to the floor and proceeded to grab the Spain defender by the throat before pushing Gavi to the ground a few seconds later, which resulted in the Argentine getting a red card.

‌



There was more drama as Nahuel Molina appeared to take a swipe at Rodri as the Spain star began celebrating, while Argentina coach Roberto Ayala allegedly threw a punch at Dani Olmo before Garcia stepped in to split them apart.

Argentina fans go wild as pilot tells them they've won World Cup in brutal prank READ MORE :

Enzo Fernandez breaks silence after World Cup final red card with message to Argentina fans READ MORE :

This has resulted in FIFA launching an investigation into the behaviour of the Argentina players and staff following the defeat to Spain in the World Cup final - with potential bans and fines now facing them.

Less than 24 hours after their defeat in New Jersey, some Argentina players have taken to social media to issue a message to the country’s supporters. However, none seemed to mention what happened after the final whistle at MetLife Stadium.

‌



Enzo Fernandez, who was sent off before the end of the 90 minutes, wrote: "As time passes, you realize there is something much bigger than a result.

"For years, this group has represented our country in the best possible way.

"It teaches that competing isn’t just about winning, but about giving everything for the shirt and never giving up. Being part of this group, which has always stood up, competed to the very end, and defended these colours with pride, humility, and commitment, is something I’ll always cherish.

‌



"I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for your affection, for your unconditional support, and for making us feel at home no matter where we are in the world.

"Wearing my country’s shirt is the greatest honour of my career, and I will continue to give everything I have every time I’m called upon to defend it."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Inter Miami star Rodrigo De Paul, meanwhile, took the opportunity to take a swipe at claims Argentina were given preferential treatment by referees and FIFA at the tournament. He wrote on Instagram, translated from Spanish: “The deepest pain comes from not being able to bring the World Cup trophy back to our country once again, because if anyone deserved to experience that feeling again, it was you.

“But as the hours pass, I’m realising that the bond you share with this team goes far beyond the trophy itself—and that is what I’m holding onto to help me get through this moment.

“Today, I look at how many people were waiting for this fall, spreading baseless conspiracy theories throughout the World Cup just to soothe their own pain at not being able to experience what we Argentines were living through—because our smiles bother them, because our ways get under their skin... But all that did was reaffirm that the passion and love for our jersey can overcome anything.

‌



“It will hurt for a long time, but today, more than ever, I am proud to be ARGENTINE.”

View 4 Images Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes appeared to kick Spain defender Eric Garcia (Image: (Photo by CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images))

Lionel Messi, who scored eight goals across the World Cup, wrote on Instagram: “The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal. But I also hold onto all the good things...

‌



“The matches we turned around by giving it our all—moments that will remain in our memories forever—and the support of an entire country which, combined with this group's hard work and effort, brought us back among the world's elite once again. It is hard to fully appreciate our achievement right now, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals.

“Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.

“I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship.”

‌



View 4 Images Lionel Messi was in tears after Argentina's World Cup final defeat (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur star Cristian Romero also wrote an emotional message on Instagram, which read: “And this time, it wasn't meant to be. And believe me, it hurts. It hurts deeply, because no one wanted to keep writing this beautiful story more than we did.

“We dreamed of bringing the trophy home again, but it didn't happen. But if there is one thing we will never lack, it is total commitment.

‌



“We gave it our all. We finished second, but we never stopped representing Argentina with the pride and dedication this jersey deserves.

“I am so proud and fortunate to be part of this family.

“I’m sorry we couldn't give you the joy we wanted so badly to share. We played for you—for every Argentine cheering us on from every corner of the globe. We felt that love every single day.

‌



“Today, we have to pick ourselves up. Start over. Work harder, believe more, and prepare to get this jersey back to the very top—right where we’ve placed it these past few years.

“Because finals aren't handed to you; you earn them by getting there. And this group—and whoever comes next—will keep fighting, united, with the same hope and passion as always.

“Thank you for being there. Thank you for believing. We will rise again. Because that’s what Argentina is all about. Always together.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Former Manchester City defender Nicolas Otamendi, who was also involved in some heated scenes with Rodri post-match, was another player who admitted the defeat has left him pained. He said: “It wasn’t the ending we dreamed of. And the truth is, it hurts deeply.

“Because behind these 50 days lay sacrifices, hugs, tears, hope, and a group that gave absolutely everything for this jersey.

‌



“But if there is one thing I will carry with me forever, it is the pride of having shared this journey with a group of extraordinary people—people who never stopped believing, who fought until the very last second, and who defended these colours with their hearts.

“Thank you to my teammates for every battle. And for never giving up.

View 4 Images Argentina's Paredes was at the centre of altercations after the match (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

‌



“To my family... thank you for always being my rock. Through every joy and every setback. You are my safe haven when football brings me its greatest thrills and its deepest sorrows.

“And thank you to the people of Argentina. Thank you for believing, for standing by us, and for making us feel your love in every corner of the globe.

“Today, we return with broken hearts, but with the peace of mind that comes from having given our all. Because finals are won or lost, but there are jerseys you defend for a lifetime.

‌



“And this one—we defended it until our very last breath. Argentina, always.”

Lautaro Martinez, who scored the goal that knocked England out of the World Cup in the semi-final, also wrote: “We gave it our all; for the second World Cup in a row, we reached the final, but this time it just wasn't meant to be.

‌



“I am so proud to be Argentine. I would have liked to try and help the team out on the pitch yesterday, but oh well.

“Thank you to everyone who supported us throughout this World Cup—travelling kilometre after kilometre to be close to us—and to everyone who cheered us on from every corner of our country.”

Lastly, Lyon defender Nicolas Tagliafico also wrote a message on social media, where he stated: “It hurts a lot, I won't deny it.

‌



“But having reached another final and giving everything on the court can't be erased by anything. Proud to be part of this group that gave it all.

“Thanks to all the Argentinians for accompanying us every step of this World Cup. You made us feel your support from the first to the last day. Let's go Argentina, always.”

There has, however, been no public apology from the Argentine players for the way they behaved post-match, with Paredes' mother even standing up for. Speaking at the Ezeiza airport in Buenos Aires, she said: "We never disrespect anyone. Respect always, I think that's everything that motivates us and gets us to where we really want to go. I know what the Argentine National Team means to my son."

Sports.title: Liverpool can only make ONE specific signing thanks to Premier League rule
Sports.content:
Liverpool can only make ONE specific signing thanks to Premier League rule

Liverpool could find it a tad tough to make new signings in the window this summer

View 3 Images (Image: Andrew Powell, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool's recruitment team is staring down a logistical headache during this summer's transfer window, as current squad limits mean they have space to register just one more senior non-homegrown player. The Premier League strictly mandates that a maximum of 17 spots within a 25-man senior squad can be allocated to overseas talent.

‌



As things currently stand, the Anfield outfit could easily completely max out their 25-man squad, boasting a breakdown of nine homegrown individuals alongside 16 non-homegrown players.

‌



If they wish to bring in multiple international reinforcements, the Reds' front office will have to pull off some highly strategic squad management, and likely facilitate a few departures, in the coming months.

‌



The nine homegrown players currently registered at Liverpool are: Joe Gomez, Curtis Jones, Harvey Elliott, Conor Bradley, Stefan Bajcetic, James McConnell, Vitezslav Jaros, Jeremie Frimpong (who qualifies through his time at Manchester City's academy) and Freddie Woodman.

The club's 16 non-homegrown players comprise: Alisson Becker, Giorgi Mamardashvili, Virgil van Dijk, Kostas Tsimikas, Milos Kerkez, Wataru Endo, Florian Wirtz, Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch, Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo, Federico Chiesa, Calvin Ramsay, Hugo Ekitike and new arrival Victor Munoz.

All 37 World Cup pundits ranked as BBC vs ITV winner decided and unexpected star emerges READ MORE :

According to the Premier League, a homegrown player is defined as someone who, regardless of nationality or age, has been registered with any club affiliated to The Football Association or the Football Association of Wales for a period, whether continuous or not, of three complete seasons, or 36 months, prior to their 21st birthday, or the conclusion of the season in which they turn 21.

‌



Regulations stipulate that players who will be classified as under-21s for the 2026/27 season are those born on or after January 1 2005.

View 3 Images Rio Ngumoha during the Premier League game between Liverpool and Brentford. (Image: Jack Thomas/Getty Images)

Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and new recruit Jeremy Jacquet remain on the entirely unrestricted Under-21 list owing to the fact they were born on or after January 1 2005. While it appears challenging for Andoni Iraola to bolster his squad this summer, the Under-21 Loophole serves as a significant get-out clause.

‌



This means Liverpool can still purchase as many foreign players as they wish this summer, provided those players were born on or afterJanuary 2005 1. Under-21 players do not require registration on the senior 25-man squad list and sidestep the 17-player non-homegrown cap.

For instance, should Liverpool sign 19-year-old Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, born in November 2006, it would have no bearing whatsoever on their remaining slots. The club could additionally still manage to bring in multiple senior foreign players, so long as they sell, loan out, or de-register players currently occupying those 16 slots.

The likes of Federico Chiesa, Wataru Endo, Alisson Becker, Giorgi Mamardashvili and even Cody Gakpo have all been linked with departures from Anfield this summer. Each time a player moves on, a brand new senior non-homegrown slot becomes available.

‌



There is also a common misconception that a club must field eight homegrown players to fill the remaining spots in their squad. This is not the case in the Premier League, though UEFA do stipulate a fixed number of "locally trained players" in the group.

View 3 Images Harvey Elliott in training with Liverpool's U21s ahead of the start of pre-season (Image: Getty Images)

With Elliott, McConnell, Ramsay, Jones and Bajcetic all facing uncertain prospects at Anfield this summer, however, the Reds may also need to bolster their homegrown quota.

‌



A solution does exist, with 21 homegrown-eligible players currently on the club's books. Yet few of those, if any at this point, appear ready to step up to first-team level.

Under Premier League regulations, though, without offloading players or omitting someone from their squad list, Liverpool can only make one further senior signing before hitting the maximum permitted 17 non-homegrown players allowed within their 25-man squad.

Sports.title: 'Wayne Rooney wants Man Utd job – but he's already found the ideal role for himself'
Sports.content:
'Wayne Rooney wants Man Utd job – but he's already found the ideal role for himself'

Ex-Manchester United star Wayne Rooney has hinted at a return to management after spells with Derby and Birmingham City

View 3 Images Wayne Rooney has been a hit on the BBC this summer (Image: BBC)

Wayne Rooney may harbour ambitions of working at Manchester United in the dugout, but it's clear he has found his niche elsewhere: in punditry. United's all-time top scorer has been something of a revelation across the BBC's World Cup coverage this summer.

‌



His no-nonsense approach, coupled with a down-to-earth take on the game, has won him a legion of fans. While Rooney clearly has the know-how should he wish to step back into management, it's perhaps the punditry life that best suits the former Everton striker.

‌



It's fair to say that Rooney's managerial career didn't hit the highs the Liverpudlian would have envisaged for himself. Spells at Derby, Birmingham, DC United and Plymouth Argyle saw him fail to claim any silverware, while he oversaw the Rams' relegation to League One in 2022.

‌



Previously, Rooney said he would only return to coaching if he was offered a position among Michael Carrick's coaching staff at Manchester United.

Rooney told BBC Sport: "Of course, I've never closed doors and never say never, but at the moment – where I am now, where my head space is – I wouldn't."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Gabby Logan escapes wrath of annoyed viewers after BBC makes change for World Cup final READ MORE :

Pressed on if he would join Carrick at United, he added: "Of course I would. It's a no-brainer. I'm not begging a job here by the way. Just so everyone knows, if I was asked to go in of course I would."

Ever since turning to a role in the media in several years ago, he impressed with his savvy takes and bagged a role on Match of the Day in 2025.

Would the ex-England star really wish to trade in life in the media for the stress of the touchline? There are many on social media hoping he doesn't, judging by their reaction to Rooney's role as an analyst.

‌



"Wayne has been spot on on a lot of things lately. This is the best version of him," one fan posted on X. Another added: "Wayne Rooneys [sic] review of the half time show was worth every penny of my licence fee." A third said: "A real revelation of this World Cup has been Wayne Rooney's skill as a pundit."

View 3 Images Wayne Rooney on the BBC's coverage of Mexico vs England (Image: BBC)

The affection for Rooney perhaps stems from his ability to call it as he sees. He's not afraid to say what many are thinking, a virtue in a media landscape that can prioritise its relationship to top stars and managers over dropping some home truths.

‌



Such unfiltered honesty can sometimes manifest itself as being offensive for the sake of it, but this isn't Rooney's style.

Case in point: The former Everton forward won a few more fans on Sunday night during the BBC's coverage of the World Cup with a take that was funny, relatable, but not uncouth.

After the 27-minute long half-time show from the likes of Justin Bieber, Rooney said: "I'll be honest, mine (highlight) was when it finished. I like lot of those artists but I thought it was crap."

‌



There is a desire among football fans to see ex-players who have scaled the heights of the game, such as Rooney, rather than TikTok and YouTube stars on their televisions. While many amateur tacticians have plenty to offer, nothing can quite replicate the thoughts of someone who has battled it out for 90 minutes at the likes of Old Trafford or Anfield.

Former Liverpool midfielder Graeme Souness, an ex-player whose punditry was also praised for its unflinching nature, is a fan.

View 3 Images Wayne Rooney lasted just 15 games with Birmingham City (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I like listening to Wayne Rooney as a pundit because he talks common sense," Souness told The Daily Mail. "I love Wayne Rooney as a player, and I like to listen to him – he has got authority, so I can listen to him. Some of the other pundits, I turn the sound down."

While the dugout could still hold a place for Rooney, for now, he has found his calling. Speaking to the BBC in August 2025, he gave a truthful appraisal of his skills as a pundit.

As expected, it was harsh but fair. "I think I'm quite fair and honest really - that is the only way to be," he said. "I say this as a player, a manager and now as a pundit - it's the same values.

Article continues below

"The fans aren't stupid. If you expect me to sit there and try and sugar-coat things which fans can see, I don't think I should be doing it."

Sports.title: Man Utd’s failed transfers for five-time Champions League winner and two World Cup heroes
Sports.content:
Man Utd’s failed transfers for five-time Champions League winner and two World Cup heroes

Manchester United are continuing to make moves in the summer transfer window ahead of the upcoming Premier League campaign

View 6 Images Michael Carrick is working hard on transfers (Image: Kirill KUDRYAVTSEV / AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester United notably let a future World Cup winner and one of England's most lethal strikers escape their grasp. The club have overseen some remarkable transfers down the years, attracting many successful players to Old Trafford.

‌



However, United have watched some promising talents choose other Premier League clubs and further afield. Michael Carrick has secured deals for Andrey Santos, Karl Darlow and Youri Tielemans this summer.

‌



Talks with Atalanta's Ederson hit a roadblock after a medical flagged up knee issues. Carrick is determined to prevent any more transfer setbacks as he assembles a squad capable of competing for trophies.

‌



Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the botched transfers at United, including a Ballon d'Or winner and World Cup champion.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Lisandro Martinez in floods of tears as Man Utd star suffers World Cup final agony READ MORE :

Ronaldinho

United came within touching distance of a £9million swoop for Ronaldinho from Paris Saint-Germain in 2003. The Brazil star had shone in France, recording 44 goal contributions across 77 outings.

‌



The midfielder was viewed as David Beckham's successor, who appeared destined for a move to Spain. Barcelona had opened discussions with the England skipper over a £30m transfer and Real Madrid were also circling.

View 6 Images Ronaldinho almost joined United (Image: Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Madrid ultimately secured Beckham for around £25m, yet Barca managed to swoop in and snatch Ronaldinho from under United's noses. United were "99.9% certain" the World Cup winner would sign but the Spanish giants pipped them to his signature for £25.5m.

‌



The Brazilian would go on to claim the Ballon d'Or in recognition of his outstanding performances in Spain.

John Obi Mikel

John Obi Mikel snubbed United in favour of Chelsea, despite holding talks with Sir Alex Ferguson and even penning a pre-contract. Speaking on TNT Sports' What I Wore, the Champions League winner said: "My first trial was with Manchester United. After the Under-17 tournament, I went there for trials. And then United thought, 'Spend two, three months with us, and then go back home, and come back. And when you become 18, you can sign a professional contract.'

"So I went back home and then Chelsea heard about the whole thing, that I was back home. And they sent an agent to Nigeria to come and get me to go to trials at Chelsea. I went to trials at Chelsea and they liked me and wanted me to sign. So they thought, 'Okay, we're not going to make the same mistake as United by sending you back home. We're going to send you to Norway'. United went to find out where I was, and then they sent an agent to come to Oslo.

‌



View 6 Images John Obi Mikel's United move was all but confirmed before the Blues swooped in (Image: ADRIAN DENNIS / AFP via Getty Images)

"That's when the contract came from United, Fergie and his agents. That's when I signed the contract. But of course, Chelsea had sent me to Norway and they said, 'Why would you do that? We've been looking after you for about a year now.' So when they saw that [I'd signed for United] they refused to let it go and said they'd fight. FIFA couldn't sort it out and get either team to back off, the English FA got involved and then I had a one-to-one meeting with Fergie.

"He said he wanted a meeting with me, alone without anybody for 30 minutes, and that he would be able to convince me to come to Manchester United. So I had the meeting, but he couldn't convince me and that's how it was settled."

‌



Toni Kroos

Toni Kroos verbally agreed to join United from Bayern Munich in 2013 as David Moyes stepped into Fergie's shoes at Old Trafford. The Germany international was considered a top target but remained in his home country for a further season before making the switch to Real Madrid.

View 6 Images Toni Kroos became a European giant in his own right (Image: Michael Regan - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Moyes told talkSPORT in 2018: "Toni Kroos had agreed to come to Manchester United with me. I met him and his wife and we agreed it all when he was at Bayern Munich."

‌



Kroos went on to claim the World Cup with Germany in 2014 and won the Champions League five times at Madrid.

Paulo Dybala

In 2019, United attempted to orchestrate a swap deal with Juventus featuring Paulo Dybala and Romelu Lukaku. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer believed the Belgium international wasn't needed and reports from Italy suggested an agreement had been reached between the sides.

View 6 Images Paulo Dybala was subject to a potential swap deal (Image: Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

‌



Dybala eventually decided to stay with Juve and won 11 major honours in Italy. He was also included in the Argentina side that lifted the World Cup in 2022 and currently plays for Roma.

Alan Shearer

Alan Shearer had his choice of Newcastle and Manchester in 1996 following his Premier League triumph with Blackburn Rovers. The division's all-time leading marksman sat down with Sir Alex and his childhood hero, Kevin Keegan, who proved pivotal in the forward's eventual decision.

View 6 Images Alan Shearer could've been a Red Devil (Image: Shaun Botterill/Allsport/Getty Images/Hulton Archive)

‌



He revealed on The Rest is Football podcast in 2023: "I had the choice between Newcastle and Man United. I went to meet Kevin and Sir Alex on the same day, I met Kevin in the morning, Sir Alex in the afternoon. And the first words in the afternoon, Sir Alex came in and said to me, 'Am I meeting you first or am I meeting you second?'

"And I said, 'I've just met Kevin this morning,' and he said, 'That's me f*****, I've got no chance.' I asked why and he said, 'Always first impressions last.' Anyway, a day went over, I went home and I said, 'I'm signing for Man United.'

"Fergie was incredible, we went to Manchester and we went house hunting. Then two days later, I got a call off Kevin to say, 'I would like an hour with you before you go and that's it.' I had talks with him and I rung my Mrs up and said, 'I'm signing for Newcastle, there's a taxi coming in half an hour, you need to pack a bag for me and we're flying to the far east tonight.'"

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Yan Diomande transfer U-turn and club issue statement over arrival
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Yan Diomande transfer U-turn and club issue statement over arrival

The Liverpool latest focuses on RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande as the Reds make a statement

View 3 Images Yan Diomande is being linked with various clubs this summer (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

Liverpool's pre-season has intensified with the club jetting out to the United States on Monday. While not all of his players were on the plane, with some players set to join later on due to their involvement in the World Cup, the next few weeks will give new head coach Andoni Iraola the best look yet at his squad.

‌



The World Cup came to an end on Sunday night. The tournament has dominated the summer, putting transfer business on the back burner for some clubs, including the Reds.

‌



However, with time ticking away until Liverpool face Newcastle United on August 23, the club's transfer business is set to ignite. Today's latest around the Reds sees Iraola confirm a new arrival, while elsewhere, a long-term Reds' target has been at the centre of a possible transfer U-turn.

‌



Liverpool confirm new arrival

Alejandro Rosalen has been confirmed as Liverpool's new first-team goalkeeping coach after the departure of Xavi Valero. The Spaniard has moved to the Reds after five years with Napoli, in which he was part of two Serie A title victories, in 2022/23 and 2024/25.

His career began at Valencia and was followed by one season in Hungary with Videoton. He spent eight years with Fiorentina before he took up the position at Napoli in 2021.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Valero told Liverpool before the end of last season that he wished to leave, just 12 months after rejoining the club from West Ham. As per The Athletic, his exit was unrelated to Arne Slot's dismissal and was believed to be a mutual decision.

View 3 Images Alejandro Rosalen has joined Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Valero was part of Rafael Benitez’s backroom staff at Anfield between 2007 and 2010. After spells at Inter, Chelsea, Napoli and Real Madrid, he spent seven years at the Hammers before being hired by Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes last summer.

‌



In a statement on the club's website announcing the new arrival, Liverpool said: "Alejandro Rosalen has been appointed as Liverpool’s new first-team goalkeeping coach. The 49-year-old Spaniard joins Andoni Iraola’s backroom staff, replacing Xavi Valero, who has now departed the Reds after a second spell with the club in 2025-26.

"Rosalen arrives on Merseyside with a wealth of experience as a goalkeeper coach. His most recent position was at Serie A side Napoli, from 2021 to this summer. While there, Rosalen contributed to Napoli lifting the Scudetto on two occasions (2022-23 and 2024-25).

"He had previously spent eight years with Fiorentina in Italy, a period that followed a single season at Hungarian outfit Videoton. Rosalen’s coaching career had begun in Valencia’s academy, where he stayed for eight years."

‌



Transfer U-turn

Long-time Liverpool target Yan Diomande was reported to have agreed personal terms with Paris Saint-Germain as far back as June. However, crucially, there’s no agreement in place between PSG and the player's club, RB Leipzig, yet, with the German side still hoping to keep the teenager.

View 3 Images Yan Diomande has made his decision (Image: Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Despite making it clear to Leipzig they could afford his apparent £86.8million asking price, the Bundesliga club held firm. Fabrizio Romano has now claimed that several other teams are still trying to muscle in on the deal to take Diomande to PSG as well, which could see the player U-turn on his decision to join the Ligue 1 outfit. However, it's unclear if Liverpool have revisited their interest.

Sports.title: 'Fery can improve but that's exciting' - Henman optimistic as Brit eyes US Open run
Sports.content:
British No 1 Arthur Fery will head into the American hard-court swing with areas he can improve ahead of the US Open - but that's "exciting", says Tim Henman.

The wild card's surprise run to the Wimbledon semi-finals has injected a much-needed shot of positivity and given British fans a new name to follow in the Grand Slams - starting at the US Open in New York - live on Sky Sports Tennis from August 30.

The challenge for the 24-year-old now is to acclimatise to his new standing in the game and the loss of anonymity and the freedom that brings with it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery reflects on his Wimbledon experience, his massive climb up the world rankings and the tournaments he's planning to play next

The 23-year-old, who has soared to 36 in the world from No 114, was the last player standing in what was an otherwise dismal tournament for the host nation, but he became only the fifth British man this century to reach the second week at the All England Club.

Fery has earned direct entry to a Masters event for the first time in Cincinnati - 13-23 August - before appearing at the Winston-Salem Open from 23-29 August ahead of his debut at Flushing Meadows.

Speaking at Royal Birkdale ahead of The Open, Henman called Fery's dream run at the All England Club "amazing" and "transformational for his career and his life".

The former British No 1 said: "He started the year at 185 in the world, qualified in Melbourne and then has continued to improve his ranking - then getting a wild card at Wimbledon ranked 114 and winning five matches getting to the semi-finals it was an incredible performance - and I think it also shows the fine margins between these top players.

"If you're in the top 250 in the world you're an extremely good player and on your day you've got a chance of beating anyone, so huge for him to be 36 in the world now getting to the other Grand Slams and Masters 1000, so he's got an opportunity to really plan his schedule moving forward."

Sports.title: Arsenal, Chelsea and Man Utd target Scott rejects new Bournemouth contract
Sports.content:
Alex Scott has turned down a new Bournemouth contract amid strong interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United, Sky Sports News understands.

Bournemouth have made Scott a number of offers since discussions began towards the end of the season - but it is believed the midfielder has indicated he is not currently willing to agree new terms.

The Cherries do not want to sell the talented midfielder, who has entered the final two years of his current contract, and have already knocked back inquiries from the Premier League trio.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd discusses Alex Scott's future after the midfielder rejected a new Bournemouth contract

United, Chelsea and Arsenal are believed to remain the frontrunners for Scott, who travelled to the States with the England squad ahead of the World Cup, while other clubs are also keen.

Bournemouth expect Scott to remain their player next season whether he signs a new offer or continues on his current deal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports senior reporter Rob Dorsett spends the day with Bournemouth's Alex Scott where he takes a closer look at the life of a Premier League footballer

It is part of their club-wide stance to keep their best players, which also includes Junior Kroupi and winger Rayan - two more players who have interest from other clubs.

Analysis: How good is the 'Guernsey Grealish'?

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

It has been the summer where midfielders are hot property.

Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Youri Tielemans have all made Premier League moves in this transfer window - the majority of them going for huge fees.

Alex Scott is another player who could expect a move this summer. The huge interest from the so-called 'Big Six' is absolutely no surprise.

Scott very nearly made England's World Cup squad this summer with Thomas Tuchel revealing earlier this summer that he was unlucky to miss out. A stellar Premier League season was behind that claim.

Scott ranks very highly in the defensive metrics among Premier League midfielders. But he is not just a defensive option. Affectionately named 'The Guernsey Grealish', Scott has superb dribbling ability and timing - as seen with his match-winning goal against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in April.

Given £116m signing Anderson has already gone, Scott is not a bad alternative option for the big clubs.

"Because if you are a young player and you do steps - and nowadays it happens many times - too fast, too quick, then it's getting difficult. The club is doing a lot of things to show the players that they are in the right place.

"So far, it's not a challenge for me, to be honest. The first four days, we are in touch and my feeling is that the boys are feeling really good here.

"Kroupi made great improvement last season, so I think for him there's no ceiling. Even he knows that he's in a good place to improve.
