World.title: Iraq reaches major agricultural milestone with first Super S potato seeds
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has achieved a major scientific and strategic breakthrough, marking a first for the nation’s agricultural sector. On Monday, July 20, 2026, the ministry officially announced that its Department of Horticulture successfully produced “Super S” grade potato seeds—the highest internationally recognized classification for potato seed quality.

The milestone was confirmed after the locally developed seeds passed exhaustive rigorous testing conducted by the Seed Testing and Certification Department, proving their absolute alignment with top global standards.

The strategic project was executed under the auspices of Minister of Agriculture Abdul Rahim Al-Shammari and directly supervised by the Director General of the Horticulture Department, Hatem Karim Al-Ghazi. The production represents the culmination of years of intensive research and practical field applications managed by the technical and scientific cadres of the National Potato Development Program.

Specialized operations spanned multiple laboratory and field stations, relying heavily on the Tissue Culture Unit in Nineveh Governorate and the Upper Euphrates Station in Anbar Governorate to ensure the harvest of genetically pure, disease-free, and virus-free national seed stocks.

Strategic Impact of the National “Super S” Seed Production

Securing Food Sovereignty: Establishing the local production of this top global seed classification acts as a foundational step toward building a sustainable, entirely domestic system for potato cultivation inside Iraq.

Reducing Import Reliance: The initiative directly aims to limit the country’s dependence on expensive imported foreign seeds, granting the agricultural sector greater autonomy over an essential crop.

Boosting the National Economy: Transitioning to domestic production will dramatically lower overall cultivation costs for local farmers while saving vital hard currency reserves that were previously spent on international seed procurement.

Maximizing Crop Yields: The high genetic purity and complete absence of viral strains inherent in “Super S” seeds directly optimize agricultural efficiency, significantly raising the production output per dunam.

This pivotal shift in seed infrastructure serves as a major pillar supporting the sustainable development strategies that the Ministry of Agriculture aims to replicate across other primary food crops.

The tangible results of this achievement are projected to positively impact local markets over the coming harvest seasons, offering Iraqi consumers and farmers a premium, highly competitive national product that stabilizes the domestic supply chain.

World.title: The Tehran test: PM Al Zaidi to demand militia disarmament in Iran visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Fresh off his diplomatic trip to Washington and a brief stopover in Doha, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi is preparing to land in Tehran on July 23, 2026. The high-stakes visit, highlighted in an analytical report by Al-Mada newspaper, is being viewed as the ultimate litmus test for the sovereign promises al-Zaidi made directly to U.S. President Donald Trump regarding domestic stability and the rule of law.

While historical precedent has typically seen Tehran serve as the mandatory protocol stop for incoming Iraqi prime ministers immediately following a White House invite, al-Zaidi’s itinerary carries deep tactical friction. Well-informed political sources reveal that the Prime Minister will formally ask the Iranian leadership to exert direct, decisive pressure on its allied domestic armed factions to surrender what intelligence circles call the “ballistic card.”

Specifically, Baghdad is demanding that these non-state groups hand over a hidden arsenal estimated to include at least eight ballistic missiles and hundreds of kamikaze drones before the September 30 legal deadline set by the federal cabinet to permanently eradicate unauthorized weapons.

High-Stakes Geopolitical Itinerary: Post-Washington Matrix

The Disarmament Deadline: September 30 remains the definitive federal cutoff for independent armed factions to integrate or fully surrender heavy arms to state control.

The Hidden Arsenal: Intelligence estimates indicate that renegade factions continue to conceal hundreds of localized drones alongside at least 8 Iranian-supplied ballistic missiles.

The Diplomatic Pre-Run: Preparations peaked in Baghdad on Monday, July 20, as Deputy Foreign Minister Muhammad Hussein Bahr al-Uloom met with Iranian Ambassador Iraj Masjedi to iron out the security agenda.

The Shifting Route: Al-Zaidi adjusted his post-US economic tour, inserting Doha and Tehran ahead of upcoming investment summits in Turkey (July 28) and Saudi Arabia to address the security crisis first.

The political stakes for the Prime Minister could not be higher. During his five days in the United States, al-Zaidi secured forty-eight monumental agreements and memorandums of understanding valued at nearly $60 billion—spanning energy deals with Chevron and ExxonMobil, digital infrastructure with Starlink, and an initial compliance framework with the U.S. Treasury to rehabilitate seven restricted domestic banks.

However, diplomatic experts and strategic analysts, including Ihsan Al-Shammari, a professor of international politics at Baghdad University, warn that any failure by al-Zaidi to decisively strip these rogue factions of their heavy weapons will trigger immediate economic blowback from Washington, potentially freezing the multi-billion-dollar corporate contracts.

Al-Shammari pointed out that the volatile drone and missile strikes launched against the Kurdistan Region late Friday night were not merely extensions of the broader U.S.–Iran conflict, but functioned as “preemptive rejection messages” from hardline local factions aiming to destabilize al-Zaidi’s administration.

Intelligence reports obtained by Al-Mada suggest that Baghdad is already moving toward a highly anticipated anti-terror sweep codenamed the “Decisive Operation.” The federal government has reportedly finalized arrest warrants for the specific factional leaders behind the recent Erbil and Sulaymaniyah breaches, vowing to publicly broadcast their identities and utilize proactive preemptive detentions if renegade cells attempt to target foreign oil conglomerates, diplomatic missions, or state bases in the coming days.

World.title: US-Iran strikes: latest developments
World.content:
Dubai – Iran’s president said his country is fighting a “full-scale war” with the United States, as Washington expanded its strikes across the Islamic republic and Tehran hit Gulf states.

Here are the latest developments on Monday:

– Yemen’s Houthis announce Saudi blockade –

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels announced a maritime embargo of Saudi Arabia, after the two adversaries traded fire last week for the first time in years.

– Iran says in ‘full-scale war’ with US –

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country was in a “full-scale war” with the United States and that Tehran should “accept the natural consequences of this resistance”.

– Iran minister to visit Pakistan –

Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni is set to travel to mediator Pakistan’s capital Islamabad on Monday, a Pakistani interior ministry source said.

The source confirmed to AFP that the minister would have talks with Pakistani officials but did not elaborate on whether it was linked to Pakistan’s long-running mediation efforts to end fighting between the United States and Iran.

– Bahrain, Kuwait report Iran attacks –

Bahrain’s civil aviation body said Iran had targeted its air navigation systems with drones, though traffic remained unaffected.

Kuwait, which like Bahrain hosts US military installations, also reported intercepting Iranian attacks.

– Oil retreats after hitting month-high –

Oil fell back after hitting its highest price in a month as Iran said diplomatic exchanges with the United States were ongoing via mediators despite the two sides’ ceasefire all but collapsing.

The benchmark Brent North Sea contract rose above $91 a barrel before giving up the gains on hopes for negotiations.

– Iran says talking to US through mediators –

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said diplomatic exchanges are going on with the United States through mediators.

“The diplomatic apparatus has been active in recent days and ideas have been conveyed to us by certain mediators,” he said.

Baghaei said Iran would not allow the Strait of Hormuz to be used to threaten the country’s security. He also called on the UN atomic agency to condemn US strikes which he said targeted the Darkhovin nuclear plant being built in southwest Iran.

– US widens strikes on Iran –

The United States expanded its strikes on Iran, targeting provinces around the country including the city of Bushehr, which hosts a nuclear power plant.

Since the resumption of hostilities, the US had focused strikes around Hormuz, but extended them on Monday to other provinces, according to state media and local authorities.

Iranian state media said at least one person was killed and several more wounded in US strikes in the country’s northwest overnight.

– Iran using Hormuz as ‘leverage’: Rubio –

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran is using the strategic Strait of Hormuz as leverage, urging other countries to step up pressure to protect global shipping.

“It’s clear that Iran, at least some people in Iran, want to control the straits and hold that as leverage against the world,” Rubio told reporters.

– Trump says US hitting Iran to honour Americans killed –

US President Donald Trump said Sunday the latest military strikes on Iran were being carried out in honour of US service members killed in recent days.

“We hit them very hard again tonight, and we did that in honour of the, probably three, it’s probably three great patriots,” Trump told reporters.

Two were killed in Jordan on Friday and a third in Iraq on Sunday, according to US officials, taking the total of confirmed American fatalities since the start of the war in February to 17.

World.title: Scars of war linger on Syria’s Saint Simeon monastery
World.content:
Dayr Sim’ān – Near the base of a column atop which Saint Simeon Stylites once perched, scattered stones lay bare the damage inflicted on the surrounding Byzantine monastery in northern Syria by war, looting and rampant illegal excavations.

AFP accompanied a French archaeological delegation to inspect the site after more than a decade of conflict and assess what could be restored.

The fifth-century monastery and its church are, alongside hundreds of abandoned ancient villages in northern Syria known as the “dead” or “forgotten cities”, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Holding her camera and notebook, archaeologist Micheline Kurdi walked through the ruins to document the site’s state and plan the first “quick interventions” to restore it, she told AFP.

“There is irreparable damage in the monastery in the southeastern section, but on the other hand the church is standing firm and in good condition,” the 42-year-old French-Syrian said.

Inside the monastery, AFP journalists saw cracked arches and partially collapsed stone walls, while the monks’ living quarters remained intact.

– ‘Rebuild it’ –

Syria was once an archaeologist’s paradise, home to some of the oldest and best-preserved jewels of ancient civilisations.

Following the start of the civil war in 2011, archaeological sites across the country were damaged, museums looted and historic city centres levelled.

One of the most famous cases was Palmyra, the Roman-era city in Syria’s desert with an imposing kilometre-long colonnade, where the Islamic State jihadist group launched a campaign of destruction and looting after capturing the site in 2015.

The Saint Simeon monastery itself was subjected to “looting, illegal excavation, military use and neglect”, according to site director Abdel Jalil Arabi.

It was controlled by various armed groups throughout the war, he said.

An airstrike hit the monastery in 2016, which UNESCO condemned without naming the party responsible, while it was further damaged by a major earthquake in 2023.

Arabi estimated that 30 to 40 percent of the site has been damaged, pointing to the collapse of the western arch and its columns.

As for Saint Simeon’s column, Arabi said “the base is there, but the remains of the column are scattered, and we will try to rebuild it”.

The monastery, which includes one of the oldest major churches in Christianity, was built around a column that Saint Simeon sat on for years, dedicating his life to prayer.

Kurdi, who dedicated her doctoral thesis to the monastery complex, said they needed to “review old plans” to reinstall the base of the main column “and the part that remained of it”.

– Past and future –

Jean-Baptiste Faivre, French charge d’affaires in Syria, said “this heritage is extremely important, not only for Syria’s past but also for its future”.

“There will be cooperation between the Syrian Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums and French cultural institutions to help restore and develop this site.”

Vincent Gelot from the French Catholic organisation Oeuvre d’Orient, who was also at the site, said the restoration would be carried out “with the support of donors and our partners, such as the French Embassy and the Aliph Foundation, which works to protect heritage in war-affected countries”.

“We hope that tourists and pilgrims will one day return to this place, because it still carries a message and speaks to us even today,” he added.

World.title: Plane carrying Spain’s World Cup winning team lands in Madrid
World.content:
Madrid – A plane carrying Spain’s newly crowned World Cup champions landed in Madrid on Monday, a day after their 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final in the United States.

A Spanish flag fluttered from the cockpit window as the Iberia aircraft carrying the squad taxied to the terminal at Madrid-Barajas airport at 14:30 local time (12:30 GMT) under clear blue skies.

Coach Luis de la Fuente was the first to step off the plane, followed by player of the tournament Rodri, who held the World Cup trophy aloft at the top of the stairs.

The squad were due to meet King Felipe VI at Zarzuela Palace outside Madrid before heading to the government headquarters at Moncloa Palace for a reception with Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.

The players and coaching staff will then parade through central Madrid on an open-top bus before arriving at the Cibeles square where a ceremony will be held.

Around one million people are expected to flood the streets of the Spanish capital to salute the players.

World.title: Iraqi forces destroy six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi military announced on Monday that Iraqi security forces had identified and destroyed six suspected hideouts belonging to ISIS in the northern province of Kirkuk during an air operation.

Iraq’s Joint Operations Command said in a statement that an airborne group of Special Forces carried out a rapid security operation early on Monday.

The hideouts were destroyed in precise airstrikes after field operations identified them in the Zghitun Valley area in Kirkuk, according to the statement.

The Kurdistan Region Security Agency (Asayish) also announced the arrest of two suspected ISIS militants in separate operations coordinated with Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) in Sulaymaniyah province earlier in July.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: 'Completely un-Indian': Rahul Gandhi demands PM Modi's apology over students' protest crackdown
World.content: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's silence over the police action against student protesters, calling it "un-Indian".His remarks came a day after a protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Monday saw roads blocked with demonstrators in the national capital. Police barricades were broken and protestors faced lathi and tear gas, with both accusing each other of going rogue.Speaking to reporters after meeting Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla along with opposition MPs, Rahul Gandhi said, "Modi ji has not even apologised for what happened yesterday. The youth are protesting against the education and testing system. The whole country knows that the education and testing system is hollowed out by termites.""Why is the Prime Minister silent? He should apologise to the students and stop this nonsense of thrashing students," he added.The Congress leader also accused the government of suppressing students' voices and demanded a discussion in Parliament on the examination crisis.Claiming that the Speaker had expressed his inability to allow an immediate debate, Rahul said, "The Speaker told us that to hold a discussion in Parliament, he needs the government's permission. What is happening is completely un-Indian. People are being beaten and assaulted."He said the protests reflected the frustration of young people and called "for the resignation of the home minister, the education minister and the Prime Minister.""The point is there is no way to treat the young people of this country. The young people of this country do not have opportunities; all the doors are closed; one door is open for competitive exams, which is also destroyed. These students here are complaining not just about the education system but their future," Rahul said."They are complaining because of Mr Ambani and Mr Adani, the RSS's complete takeover of the education system. This is about the future of young people. They watch Ambani's wedding and Rs 1,000 crores being spent there, while they have no money to open a business of their own. This is much bigger than education. This is students of India saying they have no future in India. This is legitimate. Dharmendra Pradhan, the home minister and the Prime Minister should resign," he added.This development comes after Rahul Gandhi, along with Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Arvind Sawant, RSP MP N K Premachandran and other opposition leaders, met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla seeking a discussion on the police action against students and the alleged examination irregularities.After the meeting, the Congress leader posted on X, "Our demand is simple: Parliament must have a detailed discussion on the brutality unleashed on students yesterday and on the government's complete lack of accountability for the examination crisis.""Students were beaten for asking legitimate questions about their own future. If Parliament cannot discuss the future of India's youth, what is it for?" he asked."The opposition will not let this be buried. We will ensure that the students' voice will be heard on the streets, and in Parliament," he added.Ahead of the day's proceedings, floor leaders of the INDIA bloc met in the chamber of Rajya Sabha Leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge to finalise their strategy for the second day of the Monsoon Session.The meeting was attended by Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Congress leaders Jairam Ramesh and K.C. Venugopal, SP's Dharmendra Yadav, NCP (SP)'s Supriya Sule, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut, JMM's Mahua Maji, and CPI(M) leaders John Brittas and P. Santhosh Kumar, among others.Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal said the opposition had demanded dedicated time in Parliament to discuss the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, the CBSE examination controversy and the police action against protesters."Along with LOP Rahul Gandhi ji and other opposition MPs, I met the Hon'ble Lok Sabha Speaker demanding that the LOP and opposition Parties be given dedicated time to raise the issue of the NEET and CBSE fiascos, the Delhi Police's violence on peaceful youth protesters yesterday, and to demand accountability from the government for these crises. We also demanded that the Education Minister give an explanation for his failures on the floor of the House," he wrote on X.The opposition's attack came after Monday's protests over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak escalated into violent clashes near Parliament.While the CJP accused Delhi Police of using excessive force against protesters, the police alleged that demonstrators turned violent after attempting to breach barricades.According to Delhi Police, 118 police personnel and 60 protesters were injured in the clashes. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke claimed that several student protesters, including minors, were assaulted during the police action and claimed that a girl sustained serious injuries and remains in critical condition at RML hospital.The issue had also disrupted proceedings in both Houses of Parliament on the opening day of the Monsoon Session, with opposition MPs repeatedly demanding discussions on the alleged paper leak and the alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement case.

World.title: Haryana government seals Shambhu border as farmers march to Delhi over India-US trade deal
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Haryana Police on Tuesday stopped farmers from entering Delhi by strengthening security at the Shambhu border, where barricades and cement blocks were placed to prevent them from travelling to the national capital for a 'Kisan Mahapanchayat' against the proposed India-US trade deal.

Hundreds of farmers from different parts of Punjab gathered at the Shambhu border carrying the flags of their respective organisations before setting out for Delhi. The day-long 'Kisan Mahapanchayat' has been organised at Kisan Ghat under the banner of the Desh Bachao Morcha.

A large police presence was deployed at the Punjab-Haryana border, while the bridge over the Ghaggar river was fenced off to stop the convoy from moving forward.

Farmer leader Sarwan Singh Pandher accused the Haryana government of preventing protesters from exercising their democratic right to march peacefully to Delhi.

He alleged that the action exposed the "true face" of chief minister Nayab Singh Saini, claiming that despite making promises to the people of Punjab, his government was blocking farmers from reaching the protest venue.

Pandher said farmers were demanding that the proposed India-US trade agreement be scrapped completely, arguing that it would harm the country's agricultural sector.





Leaders had earlier said farmers from Punjab, Haryana and several other states would participate in the Mahapanchayat. Hundreds of farmers had planned to travel to Delhi by bus.

Bharatiya Kisan Union (Shaheed Bhagat Singh) leader Tejveer Singh claimed the Haryana Police sealed the Shambhu border without giving any prior notice.

Meanwhile, Union minister Kiren Rijiju said that the govenrment "prioritised the farmers's interest" and that any FTA was signed "ensuring that these agreements serve the best interests of both the farmers and the nation".

"The Prime Minister addressed several significant issues and offered his guidance. He highlighted the successes the country has achieved in recent months and spoke about the FTAs signed with various nations. Regarding these agreements, the Prime Minister assured that the interests of farmers would be prioritised; he emphasised that no harm would come to them. He stated that the welfare of farmers remains paramount in any FTA signed with any country, ensuring that these agreements serve the best interests of both the farmers and the nation," Union minister Kiren Rijiju said while addressing media after NDA parliamentary party meeting.

The farmers' convoy began its journey from Gurdwara Sri Fatehgarh Sahib, where more than 1,000 farmers had stayed overnight before leaving for Delhi. The convoy travelled via Madhopur near Sirhind before reaching the Shambhu border.

Farmers in Kurukshetra also claimed they were stopped near Jyotisar while attempting to join the protest.

In view of the demonstrations, Haryana Police issued a traffic advisory and suggested alternate routes for commuters travelling between Punjab, Haryana and Delhi to minimise disruption.

On Monday, Bharatiya Kisan Union (Charuni) chief Gurnam Singh Charuni was detained by police in Kurukshetra while travelling to Delhi for the Mahapanchayat.

The outfit's spokesperson, Prince Waraich, alleged that Haryana Police had detained several workers to stop them from participating in the protest.

Farmers have strongly opposed the proposed India-US trade agreement, claiming it could allow cheaper agricultural imports into India, reduce the income of domestic farmers and weaken the country's agricultural economy.

They argued that the agreement could affect not only agriculture and dairy but also sectors such as industry, digital trade, e-commerce, government procurement, intellectual property rights and services.

The protesting farmers urged the Centre to abandon the proposed trade deal, saying it should protect the interests of farmers, agricultural labourers, livestock rearers, small traders and ordinary citizens.

The security arrangements at the Shambhu border were similar to those put in place in February 2024, when farmers were stopped from marching to Delhi during their agitation demanding a legal guarantee for the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops.

World.title: 'E20 petrol may cut mileage by up to 5%, but doesn't damage engines': Govt tells Parliament
World.content:
The government said the drop in mileage for some older vehicles is generally limited to around 3 to 5 per cent.

NEW DELHI: E20 petrol may reduce fuel efficiency by around 3 to 5 per cent in some older vehicles originally designed for E10 fuel, but there is no evidence that the higher ethanol blend causes widespread engine damage or vehicle breakdowns, the government informed Parliament on Tuesday.In a written reply in the Rajya Sabha, minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi said fuel economy is influenced by several factors, including driving style, vehicle maintenance, tyre pressure, wheel alignment and the use of air conditioning.The government said the drop in mileage for some older vehicles is generally limited to around 3 to 5 per cent. It added that E20 petrol offers advantages such as higher octane levels, improved resistance to engine knocking, better combustion and smoother acceleration.According to the government, E15+ petrol has been used widely across the country for more than three and a half years, while E19 and E20 fuel have been in use for over two and a half years.It said more than 20 crore two-wheelers and over 3 crore petrol cars, including vehicles manufactured before E20 compatibility standards were introduced, have been running on these fuel blends without any verified evidence linking ethanol blending to large-scale engine failures.The government also cited service records from vehicle manufacturers. It said one leading carmaker serviced 2.84 crore vehicles during 2025-26, including nearly 1.5 crore older vehicles that were not certified for E20 fuel, without reporting damage caused by the higher ethanol blend.Similarly, a leading two-wheeler manufacturer reported that vehicles running on E20 fuel did not experience a higher rate of damage than those using earlier fuel blends.The Centre said automobile manufacturers continue to honour vehicle warranties when customers use fuel that complies with E20 specifications.It also said laboratory studies and field trials found no significant differences in the performance of older vehicles. Tests covering drivability, engine starting, and the compatibility of metal and plastic components did not reveal any major concerns.The government further clarified that it has no plans to return to E0 or E10 petrol. It said maintaining separate nationwide supply chains for E0, E10 and E20 fuel across more than one lakh retail fuel outlets would increase logistics challenges, inventory requirements and handling costs.

World.title: 'We will see': CJI as Sena (UBT) moves SC challenging LS Speaker's approval of MPs' merger with Shinde faction
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

The Shiv Sena (UBT) on Tuesday approached the Supreme Court challenging Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's decision to approve the merger of its six MPs with the Shiv Sena led by Maharashtra deputy chief minister

.

Senior advocate Devadatt Kamat, appearing for the Uddhav Thackeray-led party, mentioned the matter before a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M. Pancholi, seeking an urgent hearing on Wednesday. Responding to the request, the Chief Justice said, "We will see."

Kamat told the bench that Speaker Om Birla had approved the merger of six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs with the Shinde-led Shiv Sena on July 18.

He argued that the development had wider constitutional implications, saying it had become "a national phenomenon" where MPs were joining the very parties they had contested elections against.

The petition challenges the Speaker's decision to recognise the merger, with the Uddhav Thackeray-led faction seeking the Supreme Court's intervention against the move.

What we know so far?

With the Speaker formally approving the merger, the strength of the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT) in the Lok Sabha has come down to just three MPs, while the Shinde-led Shiv Sena's tally has risen from seven to 13 MPs.





The party has now become the third-largest constituent of the NDA, after the BJP (239 MPs) and the TDP (16 MPs), overtaking Nitish Kumar's JD(U), which has 12 MPs.

Reacting to the development, Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde said the six MPs joined his party to secure development for their constituencies and not for "personal gains".

Dismissing allegations that the lawmakers were induced to switch sides with money, Shinde said the Uddhav Thackeray-led Sena needed to introspect on why its leaders were leaving the party. "These six MPs have joined us to ensure justice and development for the people who elected them. We will ensure they receive development funds and every possible support," he said.

World.title: 'Maybe education minister doesn't know how to write letter of resignation': Mahua Moitra takes dig at Dharmendra Pradhan amid student protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress MP

took a dig at education minister

on Tuesday, saying he probably does not know how to write a letter of resignation. The comment comes amid ongoing protests organised by Cockroach Janta Party demanding his resignation over

paper leaks.

"Maybe just maybe the Education Minister doesnât know how to write a letter of resignation.

RSS

only teaches you how to write mercy petitions," she wrote on X.

Her remarks came as CJP protesters continued their sit-in at Delhi's Jantar Mantar a day after police used force to stop the 'Sansad Chalo' march towards Parliament.

Despite heavy rain, tight security and Monday's crackdown, volunteers remained at the protest site on Tuesday, cleaning the stage after police removed tents and other temporary structures.

The stage canopy was left torn following the operation.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke apologised to supporters allegedly injured during the police action, particularly women protesters. In a post on X, he said, "I apologise to all our supporters, especially the girls who were brutally beaten up by male police officers. We could have done better."

Dipke also alleged that the government was willing to use force "to protect one Dharmendra Pradhan" and claimed the education minister was responsible for the deaths of more than 20 students.





He urged injured protesters to contact him personally.

Meanwhile, CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said activist Sonam Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike had entered its 24th day and reiterated the group's demand that Pradhan resigns.

The protests, which began on June 20, seek accountability over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, reforms in the education system and the resignation of the Union education minister.

Police used lathicharge and tear gas on Monday after protesters attempted to march towards Parliament, with both the protesters and the police blaming each other for the violence. Wangchuk, who was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi Police on July 18, has continued his hunger strike from the hospital.

World.title: 'Similar insensitivity on full display after one year': Congress on Dhankhar resignation
World.content:
Congress on Dhankhar resignation (ANI image)

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday criticised the Centre on the first anniversary of former Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar's resignation, alleging that he was forced to step down three years into his five-year tenure because he repeatedly spoke about the plight of farmers.In a post on X, Ramesh said Dhankhar was appointed "with great fanfare" by Prime Minister Narendra Modi but was abruptly made to resign after expressing anguish over farmers' distress and what he described as the government's "shocking insensitivity" towards them.The Congress leader said the same "insensitivity and indifference" was now visible in the government's handling of the concerns of lakhs of students and youth, referring to ongoing protests over alleged examination irregularities and demands for greater transparency in the education system."It was exactly a year ago today that the then Vice President of India and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha was forcibly made to resign just three years into his five-year tenure. He was appointed with great fanfare by the Prime Minister but was suddenly made to exit because he repeatedly expressed anguish at the plight and distress of farmers and the Modi Govt's shocking insensitivity towards them â a similar insensitivity and indifference now on full display in regard to the pressing concerns of lakhs of students and youth," Ramesh wrote.Ramesh also alleged that Dhankhar was not even given the courtesy of a formal farewell by members of the Rajya Sabha after demitting office.Jagdeep Dhankhar assumed office as Vice President in August 2022 and was due to complete his five-year term in 2027. However, on the opening day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament on July 21 last year, he unexpectedly resigned, citing health reasons.In his resignation letter to President Droupadi Murmu, Dhankhar wrote, "To prioritise health care and abide by medical advice, I hereby resign as Vice-President of India, effective immediately, in accordance with Article 67(a) of the Constitution."President Murmu subsequently accepted his resignation. Dhankhar became only the third Vice President after V V Giri and R Venkataraman to step down before completing a full term. Both Giri and Venkataraman had resigned to contest the presidential election.

World.title: 'Future of youth priority': PM Modi says NEET leak national issue, asks to avoid 'partisan politics'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister

Tuesday said PM Narendra Modi, during the NDA's parliamentary party meeting, reiterated government's stance to ensure "stringent punishment" for those involved in the NEET paper leak.

Rijiju, who is the minister of parliamentary affairs, said the Prime Minister stated that "NEET paper leak should not be an issue of partisan politics" as it is a "national issue and not a matter of one state or the Centre alone".

PM Modi, according to Rijiju, also said that "security and future of youth" is the government's priority.

The Prime Minister's reaction comes in the backdrop of protest led by youth and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) members, who were protesting against the perpetual paper leaks, and alleged irregularities in the education system.

The uproar over the NEET leak and lack of accountability at the senior-most level exploded in the Capital on Monday as protestors, mostly students and youths, clashed with police -- leading the cops to resort to lathi charge, firing of tear gas to disperse the protesting crowd marching towards the Parliament.

The protesters had three main demands: Resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, discharging Sonam Wangchuk from hospital and providing compensation to the kin of NEET aspirants who died by suicide after the leak forced the government to re-examination.





The Monday mayhem

More than 170 people, including Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protesters and Delhi Police personnel, were treated at central government hospitals on Monday following clashes during the 'Chalo Sansad' march, with a young woman admitted to Safdarjung Hospital in critical condition, sources said.

According to hospital sources, around 150 injured people were taken to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital, while at least 24 others received treatment at Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC).

Many of those brought to both hospitals were discharged after receiving first aid.

Officials at RML said that by 7 pm, the hospital's surgery department had registered 65 medico-legal cases (MLCs) involving both protesters and police personnel. They added that detailed information on all cases was still being compiled.

Hospital authorities also said around 10 MLCs involved people who had been on hunger strike.

All of them were reported to be in stable condition.

Sources at RML said nearly 40 of the injured brought to the hospital were police personnel, while the remaining patients were protesters. Around 35 people were admitted, with the rest treated and discharged. Between seven and eight patients required treatment in the hospital's red zone because of the seriousness of their injuries.

Among those admitted was a 20-year-old woman who suffered a hypoxic brain injury, a condition caused when the brain is deprived of adequate oxygen following severe trauma, hospital sources said.

The exact circumstances in which she sustained her injuries remain unclear. According to hospital sources, she may have been injured during the clashes or after falling in the stampede that followed, but the sequence of events has not yet been established.

Doctors said most of the remaining patients suffered bruises, baton injuries, head wounds and facial injuries, including split lips, forehead wounds and scalp lacerations.

Although many had visible injuries to the head and face, no fractures were reported among patients treated at RML.

At Lady Hardinge Medical College, at least 24 injured people were treated. Most were discharged after first aid, while those who arrived later in the evening continued to undergo medical evaluation. Doctors at the hospital said none of the patients brought there had sustained major injuries.

World.title: Two premier hospital RDAs seek President's intervention over Wangchuk case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A day after the Resident Doctors' Association (RDA) of

wrote to President Droupadi Murmu over the Jantar Mantar crackdown and the continued hospitalisation of climate activist

, the RDA of VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital on Tuesday also sought the President's intervention, raising concerns over patient autonomy, medical ethics, the independence of public healthcare institutions and the reported events at Jantar Mantar.

In a four-page representation, the Safdarjung RDA said Wangchuk's medical condition and the need for continued hospitalisation should remain matters of independent clinical judgement, but every competent patient is entitled to dignity, informed consent and treatment in accordance with established medical ethics and the Constitution.

The association said reports suggesting Wangchuk, despite being a competent patient, was allegedly not permitted to avail Leave Against Medical Advice (LAMA), if accurate, raise "serious concerns regarding informed consent, personal liberty and constitutional rights".

Hospitals, it said, are institutions of healing and should not be perceived as places of detention except where restrictions are authorised by law and follow due process.

The RDA also questioned the security arrangements at Safdarjung Hospital during Wangchuk's admission. Referring to reports and publicly available visuals, it said restricted access to hospital areas, extensive deployment of security personnel and disruption of routine hospital functioning, if established, warranted an independent examination.





It also called for an independent, impartial and time-bound inquiry into the reported events at Jantar Mantar, citing reports and videos indicating the use of force, including lathi charge and tear gas, against peaceful protesters. The association further referred to allegations of intimidation and physical misconduct involving faculty members and students of Lady Hardinge Medical College, saying these too required an impartial investigation.

The RDA said such incidents risk eroding public confidence in democratic and healthcare institutions and place healthcare professionals at greater risk of hostility despite having no role in administrative or political decisions. It added that hospital administrations must remain independent custodians of medical ethics and patient welfare and should never be perceived as aligned with non-medical or political interests.

Describing its appeal as "not political", the association urged the President to order an independent inquiry into the recent events, safeguard competent patients' right to seek Leave Against Medical Advice wherever legally permissible, examine whether security arrangements at Safdarjung Hospital affected patient care and hospital functioning, ensure accountability if constitutional rights or medical ethics were violated, investigate allegations of excessive force against peaceful protesters and protect healthcare professionals from intimidation and violence.

The Safdarjung RDA's representation comes a day after the AIIMS RDA sought the President's intervention over the Jantar Mantar incident and Wangchuk's continued hospitalisation, raising concerns over patient autonomy, constitutional rights and medical ethics. With Tuesday's letter, resident doctors from two of the country's premier government hospitals have now publicly sought intervention over the issue.

The representation was signed by RDA President Dr Devaunshi Kaul, Vice-President Dr Rahul, General Secretary Dr Ayush Raj, Joint Secretary Dr Amit Yadav and Treasurer Dr Rohit Rathi.

World.title: TASMAC to procure beer, IMFS equally from all suppliers
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC) will start procuring beer and India Made Foreign Spirits (IMFS) Ordinary equally from all the suppliers in the State. Earlier, liquor was procured from select manufacturers depending on which party was in power. The State has 11 distilleries and six breweries. IMFS Ordinary includes brandy and rum.

This will also be piloted at Elite Shops in seven locations including Chennai Central, South and North; Coimbatore North and South and Madurai North and South. For malls located in these locations atleast one case of every brand under the premium category shall invariably be supplied.

Officials said the board of TASMAC in its board meeting held on June 6, 2026 reviewed the existing system of indent generation and resolved that in order to ensure a more rational and equitable supply of stocks, indents shall henceforth be generated based on the sales data of Retail Vending (RV) shops instead of the existing formula adopted for depots.

Those tracking the liquor industry say this tipplers would be left with little options is this methodology is followed. “We should give what customers want. You can’t say that stock is over so you drink what you want,” an industry watcher said.

World.title: ASEAN's top diplomats meet in shadow of U.S.-Iran conflict
World.content:
Tensions between the U.S. and Iran ⁠are likely to cast a shadow over a diplomatic gathering in Southeast Asia this week, injecting additional uncertainty into a region grappling with maritime tensions with China and a faltering regional effort to end Myanmar’s civil war. Foreign ‌Ministers from the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations and major partners will gather in Manila against a backdrop of instability beyond the region since the U.S. ‌and Iran resumed open conflict, raising concerns about energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, as ‌well ⁠as inflation and global growth.

“We’re looking at several occasions where they can raise this ⁠very, very critical topic,” said Dominic Xavier Imperial, a spokesperson for the Philippines, the meeting host.

But Southeast Asia’s top diplomats meeting on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) face no shortage of challenges closer to home.

They will have an informal consultation on Myanmar’s conflict, as ​ASEAN’s peace initiative struggles to gain traction, ‌five years after it was launched following a military coup that plunged the country into a civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people.

Rubio takes aim at Beijing ahead of meeting

Likely to be discussed also are tensions in the South China Sea, for which ASEAN ‌and China are, after nearly 10 years, still trying to conclude a code of ​conduct to prevent disputes from escalating. Ahead of the gathering, U.S.-ally the Philippines accused China’s Coast Guard personnel of aggressively striking one of its navy personnel on the ⁠head with a baton near the disputed Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea on Monday. China’s Coast Guard called that “false”.

The U.S. State Department condemned what it described as China’s “dangerous and aggressive” actions, ‌in what it called “China’s troubling pattern of provocation against lawful Philippine maritime operations”. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi will join the ASEAN-led meeting in the days ahead and could meet on the sidelines. Also attending will be India, Japan, Australia, South Korea, Russia, Britain and the European Union, among others.

Without naming China, Mr. Rubio took a swipe at Beijing in an opinion piece published in Philippine newspapers upon his arrival in Manila on Tuesday, reaffirming U.S. commitment ‌to freedom of navigation, but warning such freedom was “by no means guaranteed”.

“If those waters fall under the control of ​a power willing to use commerce as a geopolitical weapon, both the United States and the ASEAN states would face dire new threats to their sovereignty, security and ⁠economic futures,” Mr. Rubio said in the piece.

Mr. Rubio reiterated a 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated China’s sweeping sovereignty claims ⁠in the South China Sea was final and binding and said the U.S. would honour its obligations to the Philippines and other allies “as they confront new and coercive threats to ‌our shared interests.”

China does not recognise the arbitration ruling, which went in favour of the Philippines.

Separately, Australia on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) announced a further $6.7 million contribution to a drones package for the ​Philippine Coast Guard to boost its maritime surveillance capacity, which includes long-range and underwater drone capabilities and training.

World.title: July 21, 1993 Kolkata police firing: What does the Commission of Inquiry report reveal? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: A day before the multiple rallies were held in Kolkata on account of Martyrs’ Day, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on July 20, 2026, made public report of Justice Susanta Chatterjee Commission of Inquiry. The Commission of Inquiry to probe the police firing on Youth Congress supporters on July 21, 1993, where 13 Congress supporters were killed was announced by former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, when she came to power in 2011.

Ms. Banerjee who was a youth Congress leader then had led the march demanding that photo-identification card be made mandatory for casting votes. The procession was to march to the State Secretariat Writers Buildings, but the police intervened and fired upon the protesters in the city’s Esplanade Area. Ms. Banerjee had sustained injuries in the police action.

What did CM Suvendu Adhikari reveal about Inquiry Commission report?

Making the Justice Susanta Chatterjee Commission of Inquiry public in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said the firing on protesters was uncalled for.

“There was no need to fire bullets to control the crowd located far away from Writers Buildings” and “apprehension of an attack on Writers’ Building was imaginary,” the Chief Minister said quoting from the report.

CM Suvendu Adhikari said that the former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, who had always claimed to be the prime witness in the July 21 firing, was not asked by the Commission to give her statement.

“The Commission, in its report, said that no proper documents were supplied to it. The former Chief Minister, Mamata Banerjee, who claimed to be the prime witness, did not record her statement before the Commission,” CM Suvendu Adhikari said.

The Chief Minister raised questions on the role of Manish Gupta, who was the Home Secretary in the then Left Front government, who later became a Cabinet Minister in the Mamata Banerjee government.

Mr. Adhikari said that the most important part of the report was the statement of Pankaj Banerjee (the former Leader of the Opposition) who refused to appear as a witness because he believed the Commission had been formed to shield the then Home Secretary (Manish Gupta) and a section of police officers,” he added.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari tried to highlight that Mamata Banerjee, and leaders of her party used the emotions of July 21 police firing to amass their personal property and political fortunes, but the families of the martyrs are being completely neglected today.

He added that while the Commission recommended ₹25 lakh as compensation for the family of each person killed and ₹5 lakh for every injured person, the families of those killed received only ₹2 lakh and the injured ₹15,000 during the previous Trinamool Congress government.

How many witnesses did the Justice Susanta Chatterjee Commission of Inquiry examine?

Justice Susanta Chatterjee Commission of Inquiry had summoned a total of 44 people including former Chief Minister (late) Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, then Chief Secretary N. Krishnamurthy and the then Home Secretary Manish Gupta, former Kolkata Police Commissioner Tushar Kanti Talukder and CPI(M) leader Biman Basu and journalists and photographers who were present when the firing occurred. The Commission had submitted its report in 2014, but the report was not made public by the Mamata Banerjee government.

The Trinamool Congress, however, observed the Martyrs’ Day with much pomp after it came to power in 2011. After 2011, when Mamata Banerjee came to power, not only her party leaders and supporters but prominent people from all walks of life would make a beeline at the July 21 Martyrs’ Day gathering. Lakhs of people from across the State would gather outside Victoria House in Esplanade to catch a glimpse of the leader and hear her speak.

What is the political significance of the Commission report’s release?

By making public the contents of the report, which was not made public by the previous Trinamool Congress government, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal is trying to claim that Mamata Banerjee was not serious about giving justice to the 13 Youth Congress supporters killed in police firing in 1993. The BJP leadership claims that the contents of the report reveal that the former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee used the incident only as a political tool to rally her supporters.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 2 LIVE: Both Houses adjourned till 2 p.m. amid uproar; Oppn. MPs seek Lok Sabha discussion on 'brutality' on students
World.content:
Both Houses are witnessing repeated adjournments minutes after beginning proceedings on day 2 of the Monsoon Session of Parliament on Tuesday (July 21, 2026). While Lok Sabha was adjourned with Speaker Om Birla asserting that issues will be raised post Question Hour, the Rajya Sabha broke into a din as soon as Leader of the House and Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge began speaking about the police crackdown on the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest and proposed Parliament march in New Delhi on Monday (July 20, 2026).

Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi along with some Opposition MPs met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) and urged him to allow a discussion in the House on the “brutality unleashed” on students and the government’s “complete lack of accountability” for the examination crisis. AAP MPs in Rajya Sabha, including Sanjay Singh, were seen outside the Parliament premises raising slogans and protesting against the crackdown.

In a move to grant statutory protection to the National Song Vande Mataram., the Centre will likely table the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026. in the Rajya Sabha on Tuesday (July 21, 2026). According to the Bill, any act causing obstruction in the singing of the National Song or insulting it in any form would become punishable under law. Meanwhile, the Lok Sabha is scheduled to take up the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, for consideration and passing.

World.title: Assam flood situation eases, death toll rises to 11
World.content:
GUWAHATI

The flood situation in Assam eased on Tuesday (July 21, 2026), but a human life was lost in the State’s Charaideo district, taking the death toll to 11 in less than a month.

An update from the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) said 3.13 lakh people remain affected across 11 districts, down from 3.63 lakh people across 16 districts on Monday (July 20, 2026).

“Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Jorhat continue to be the worst-affected districts. A person died due to floods in Charaideo district,” an ASDMA spokesperson said.

Officials in the flood-hit districts have established 52 relief camps, currently housing 12,720 people. Rescue workers evacuated 9,160 stranded people by boats.

The ASDMA also reported urban floods from six areas of Guwahati. These are Satgaon, Sawkuchi, Notboma, Boragaon, Maligaon, and Chandmari.

“Landslides were reported Monday [July 20, 2026] evening from five areas of Guwahati,” the spokesperson said.

According to data provided, the Brahmaputra River was flowing above the danger level at Neamatighat, the Buridihing River at Khowang, the Dikhou River at Sivasagar, the Disang River at Nganglamuraghat and the Dhansiri River at Golaghat and Numaligarh.

World.title: Nara Lokesh distributes land titles to 3,000 residents in Mangalagiri
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh Minister for Information Technology, Electronics, Human Resources Development Nara Lokesh distributed permanent land ownership titles to nearly 3,000 beneficiaries from Mangalagiri and Tadepalli mandals at a public meeting under the “Mana Illu, Mana Lokesh” programme at Mangalagiri near here on Tuesday (July 21, 2026).

Mr. Lokesh said the distribution fulfilled one of his election promises, to give permanent ownership rights to eligible residents. He recalled that after the 2019 Assembly election, people had repeatedly sought legal rights over the lands they had occupied for decades.

VIDEO | Mangalagiri: "TDP-led coalition govt granting permanent land rights to 3,000 families in the second phase under 'Mana Illu–Mana Lokesh' programme," says Andhra Pradesh Minister Nara Lokesh (@naralokesh).



(Source: Third Party)



(Full video available on PTI Videos -… pic.twitter.com/Zu2rUalO7B — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) July 21, 2026

“I had assured them that while it was not possible to regularise all lands immediately, I would fulfil the promise within five years if elected to power. Today, that assurance has been honoured,” he said. The Minister said the beneficiaries had lived for years with uncertainty over the security of their properties, fearing eviction. With the issuance of permanent titles, they would now have legal ownership and could use their properties as assets, including for obtaining bank loans. The total value of the lands covered under the programme is around ₹1,000 crore, he said.

Reflecting on his political journey, Mr. Lokesh said his defeat in the 2019 Assembly election by about 5,300 votes had motivated him to work harder to win the confidence of the people. He said he had appealed to voters before the 2024 election to convert that margin into a victory by “adding one more zero”, and expressed gratitude that the people had given him one of the top three victory margins in the State. "The strength and trust given by the people of Mangalagiri continue to inspire me to work harder," he said.

Highlighting development works in the constituency, Mr. Lokesh said underground drainage, 24-hour drinking water supply, parks and modern crematoriums were being developed. At the State level, he said the coalition government had implemented welfare measures such as the enhanced ₹4,000 social pension, Talliki Vandanam, Stree Shakti and Anna Canteens.

He said the government was simultaneously pursuing welfare and development despite financial constraints.

According to him, when the coalition assumed office, government expenditure far exceeded revenue. Through efforts to attract industries and restart stalled projects, the gap had narrowed, enabling the government to move towards fulfilling all election commitments.

Central support

Mr. Lokesh also spoke of the cooperation between the Telugu Desam Party, Jana Sena Party and BJP governments at the State and the Centre. He thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for extending support to Andhra Pradesh, citing assistance for the Visakhapatnam Railway Zone, the Polavaram project and Amaravati, and granting statutory backing to the capital.

He also expressed gratitude to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan for their support in the State’s development, and reiterated that the government’s focus was on creating employment opportunities for the youth while ensuring balanced development and welfare.

Emphasising transparency in the land title distribution process, Mr. Lokesh said leaders of the three alliance parties had visited beneficiaries’ homes to verify eligibility and ensure that only genuine beneficiaries received the titles.

State Padmashali Corporation chairman Nandam Abaddaiah, Jana Sena leader Chillapalli Srinivasa Rao, and senior TDP leaders Pothineni Srinivasa Rao and Vallabhaneni Venkata Rao, among others, attended the programme.

World.title: Karnataka Police Complaints Authority recommends ban on ‘Khaki Swag’ reels, uniformed social media posts
World.content:
The Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority (KSPCA) has recommended a State-wide ban on police personnel posting reels, photographs, pre-wedding shoots, and other social media content in uniform, saying the growing “Khaki Swag” trend is undermining the dignity, discipline, and public trust associated with the police force.

In a letter dated July 14, 2026, addressed to the Director-General and Inspector-General of Police (DG&IGP), KSPCA member Mohan Kumar Danappa urged the Police Department to issue strict directions prohibiting officers and personnel of all ranks from uploading photographs, videos, blogs or reels in police uniform on personal social media accounts.

The authority observed that while the police uniform symbolises discipline, integrity, duty, and public service, some personnel have increasingly been using it for personal publicity by creating reels, dance videos, pre-wedding shoots, motivational content, blogs, and videos featuring official vehicles, firearms, and other police equipment. It also expressed concern over senior officers allegedly using official duties, inspections, law and order bandobast, and crime scene visits to create promotional videos for social media.

According to the letter, such content not only affects the image of the Police Department but also exposes official premises, vehicles, weapons, and operational details, raising security concerns and potentially violating the Official Secrets Act, 1923. The authority further alleged that fraudsters have misused photographs of police officers in uniform to create fake social media accounts and cheat members of the public.

The KSPCA pointed out that several States, including Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Bihar, have already imposed restrictions on police personnel posting social media content in uniform. It also referred to a Standing Order issued by the Bengaluru City Police Commissioner on July 22, 2024, against such practices, stating that compliance has remained poor.

Among its recommendations, the authority has sought a complete ban on posting photographs, reels or videos in police uniform on personal social media accounts and using uniformed photographs as display pictures, removal of all existing photographs, videos and pre-wedding shoots in uniform from personal accounts and fan pages, continuous monitoring of police personnel’s social media accounts by the department’s social media cell and disciplinary action against violators, and strict instructions to all police academies and training centres to prohibit trainees from creating or sharing reels or photographs in uniform or displaying firearms on social media.

World.title: Odessa ship attack: Bodies of two Indian seafarers identified
World.content:
Two Indian seafarers have been identified among at least ten crew members killed when the general cargo vessel MV Golden Leo was struck by missiles while departing the Port of Odesa on Sunday (July 19, 2026). Two among the dead Indians dead have been identified as Chief Officer Akhil Jovan, 26, of Kerala, and Ordinary Seaman Abhishek Nishad, 21, of Uttar Pradesh. Both had signed on to the vessel at Istanbul on June 12.

The Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel, carrying a cargo of grain, came under attack at approximately 1600 hrs Ukraine local time as it exited the port. Three missiles struck the ship, according to official sources. A Ukrainian port pilot was on board at the time, guiding the vessel out of harbour.

Golden Leo was carrying 17 crew members — five Indian nationals and 12 Syrian nationals — besides the Ukrainian pilot. The ship was under the command of Master Ahmad Hamwia, a Syrian national.

All ten crew initially listed as missing have now been confirmed dead, and all bodies recovered. Eight of the ten remain unidentified, owing to severe burns sustained in the attack. Identification is pending through established forensic procedure. The bodies of two more Indian seafarers is feared to be among them.

Eight others, including a third Indian national serving as Third Officer, were rescued and are undergoing hospital treatment.

The Indian seafarers on board were engaged through a Navi Mumbai-based recruitment and placement service licence (RPSL) holder.

Golden Leo, built and operating under the Guinea-Bissau flag, was struck just outside the Odesa Sea Port Control area — one of the exit channels vessels use after loading at the port’s grain terminals.

World.title: Amitabh Bachchan recovering after surgery, opens up about ‘most difficult phase’
World.content:
Bollywood megstar Amitabh Bachchan took to his blog on Tuesday to inform his fans and followers that he was recently in the hospital for surgery, but has now been discharged. The 83-year-old actor opened up about his recovery and said that he is undergoing the most difficult phase “physically, psychologically and practically.”



Bachchan wrote on his blog, “.. in hospital in a surgery and in the ICU, under the care of proficient doctors and medical staff .. a discharge .. and a homecoming. This homecoming period is the most difficult phase .. physically, psychologically and practically ..”

He added, “.. you are a revered Champion and one day a defeat stares at you .. this is the most difficult phase of your life ..some brave it .. some succumb .. they that strive and be brave ever remain Champions .. they that do not , get reconciled and live, exist in the past glory .. a choice each makes individually .. nothing wrong by either .. be well be happy ..”

World.title: Yogi to Akhilesh, Mayawati to Aazad, how key UP players step up Dalit outreach for 2027 polls
World.content:
With the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections barely seven months away, all the leading contenders, including the ruling BJP and the principal Opposition Samajwadi Party (SP) as well as their allies, have intensified their attempts to reach out to the Scheduled Caste (SC) groups.

The Mayawati-led BSP and the Chandra Shekhar Aazad-led Aazad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) or ASP (KR) have also been vying with each other to consolidate and expand their support bases among Dalits in the state ahead of the polls.



A political row has erupted in the state in the wake of a Dalit college girl’s murder in Meerut in May, which has sparked protests with a demonstration turning violent on July 8. The outrage has been fuelled by the police crackdown on protesters with demands raised for action against Meerut Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Avinash Pandey for allegedly beating them.

Dalits make up 21% of UP’s population, with 84 Assembly seats of the state’s 403 seats reserved for them. In the 2022 polls, the BJP and its ally Apna Dal (Sonelal) together bagged 63 SC seats as compared to 20 won by the then SP-led alliance. Dalits are largely influential in western UP, Bundelkhand and eastern UP.

BJP

Weeks after the murder of the Meerut Dalit girl, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath met her family members at a government guest house in Ghaziabad on July 18. Consoling the bereaved family, the CM said, “No person involved in this heinous crime will be spared under any circumstances, and the strictest legal action will be ensured against all those responsible.”



Adityanath also declared a financial assistance of Rs 5 lakh and housing to the victim’s family.

Last Friday, UP minister for social welfare and SC/ST welfare, Asim Arun, former IPS officer, met the slain Dalit girl’s family in Meerut and reviewed the investigation of the case.

In April, seeking to rebuild its social coalition involving Dalits, the Adityanath-led BJP government launched a new scheme, a Rs 403-crore Dr B R Ambedkar Murti Vikas Yojana, that seeks to beautify, develop and maintain statues of Ambedkar in all 403 constituencies.

The CM also announced that symbolic “protective umbrellas” will be installed over statues of Ambedkar and other social justice icons across UP.

In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, of the UP’s 80 seats, the BJP saw its tally drop to 33 from 62 in the 2019 polls, with the SP-Congress coalition bagging 43 seats. Of the 17 SC-reserved constituencies, the SP won seven seats and the Congress one, while the BJP got eight. The remaining one reserved seat, Nagina, won by the BSP in 2019, was clinched by Chandra Shekhar Aazad.

Samajwadi Party

The Akhilesh Yadav-led SP held a “Samvidhan bachao, Loktantra bachao maha rally” and a discussion on Ambedkar’s legacy in Meerut Sunday, with the party proposing to hold similar events in other districts in the coming days.

Earlier this year, for the first time, Akhilesh decided to celebrate BSP founder Kanshi Ram’s birth anniversary on March 15 on a large scale across the state, calling it the “Bahujan Samaj Diwas or PDA (Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak) Diwas”.

“Kanshi Ram joined hands with great socialist leader Mulayam Singh Yadav in December 1992 and gave momentum to the ‘Bahujan Samaj Banao Abhiyan’. He helped form a government of oppressed sections under the leadership of Netaji (Mulayam) in December 1993,” the SP said.

SP sources say that apart from the SC seats, the party is working on a plan to give tickets to the Dalit candidates in at least 14 general seats in the 2027 elections in a move to solidify its PDA plank.

BSP

Struggling to rejuvenate the BSP which has faced debacles in both the 2022 Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, the party’s supremo and ex-CM Mayawati last year revived “bhaichara committees” to form social alliances of Dalits with Muslims and OBCs.

The BSP formed the Muslims Samaj Bhaichara Sangathan with two coordinators — one each from the Muslim and the Dalit groups. Similarly, two coordinators from the OBC and Dalit communities were included in the OBC Bhaichara committee. The party has been reviewing the functioning of these panels every month.

However, Mayawati’s stance on protests over the Meerut Dalit girl’s killing drew criticism from Aazad, who is trying to emerge as a key Dalit face in UP and other adjoining regions.

In her reaction to Meerut protests, Mayawati urged Dalits and other marginalised sections to fight injustice through constitutional means and refrain from taking to the streets, asserting that political empowerment through the ballot remains key to securing their rights. “Certain organisations and political parties, driven by narrow political interests, mislead and provoke members of oppressed communities into launching protests,” she said, in an apparent swipe at the ASP(KR).

ASP(KR)

Mayawat’s remarks on Meerut protests drew a sharp response from Aazad who visited Meerut to meet the Dalit victim girl’s mother and sister, assuring them that he will raise the matter in Parliament. In a veiled attack on Mayawati, he said that issuing statements alone was “insufficient” and that political leaders should stand with victims’ families.

In early June, Aazad launched his “Satta Parivartan Yatra” in UP to woo the Dalit voters ahead of the 2027 polls. He also started screening his party’s probable candidates for the polls.

“Whenever any incident of crime against any Dalit, Muslim and OBC happens, our leader (Aazad) reaches there to meet the victims and their families. He was recently in Meerut, Lucknow and Rae Bareli in this regard,” said Saurabh Kishore, ASP (KR) state vice-president, adding that the first list of the party candidates is likely to be released on July 21.

Congress

The Congress, a major SP ally, has also signalled a renewed focus on a Dalit-OBC coalition as the party recently replaced Avinash Pande with Rajendra Pal Gautam as the All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge of UP. A prominent Dalit leader, Gautam is also the chairman of the AICC’s SC department.

The grand old party also staked its claim on Kanshi Ram’s legacy by commemorating his birth anniversary as “Samajik Parivartan Diwas”. Addressing that programme in Lucknow, Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said if they had been alive, Jawaharlal Nehru would have made Kanshi Ram a Congress CM.

On July 20, the Congress launched the “Bahujan Vichar” campaign for holding padyatras and seminars across UP till August 20 in order to carry out mobilisation among the OBC, Dalit and other marginalised groups.

LJP (RV)

Last week the LJP (Ram Vilas), one of the BJP-led NDA’s major ally in Bihar, held its UP state executive meeting in Lucknow, which was attended by the party’s chief and Union minister Chirag Paswan. Sources said some leaders from the Pasi (Dalit) group suggested a slogan – “Kyun maange udhaar, jab apna neta taiyyar. (Why borrow leaders from other parties when we have our own leader)”.

Later, Chirag reportedly said his party was preparing for all 403 seats to contest the polls.

LJP(RV) MP Arun Bharti and party national spokesperson Dhirendra Kumar Sinha have been travelling across UP for the past one year, meeting the families of Dalits who suffered various atrocities.

“Pasi community in UP is feeling helpless. LJP(RV) is providing support and financial assistance to Dalits whenever atrocities happen to them. In most of such cases, SP leaders are accused. We take up the issues before the CM too,” Sinha said, adding that the party would organise “Dalit chaupals” at the village level in every Assembly segment.

Bharti and Sinha will attend one such event in Ayodhya on July 24. “We are consolidating our core base vote of Pasis and Paswans,” Sinha said, claiming that there was no Pasi representative in the NDA in UP.

The LJP(RV) has identified 104 seats where Pasis and Paswans are considered notable factors, who had supported the SP-Congress alliance in the 2024 elections.

World.title: ‘Save our democracy’: Shiv Sena (UBT) moves Supreme Court against MPs’ merger
World.content:
The Shiv Sena (UBT) on Tuesday moved the Supreme Court challenging Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s decision to recognise the merger of six of its MPs with the rival Shiv Sena led by Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde.

Senior Advocate Devadatt Kamat, appearing for the petitioner, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Arvind Ganpat Sawant, mentioned the matter before Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, who was presiding over a three-judge bench, and sought an urgent hearing.

“Six of these MPs decide unilaterally, without the merger of the original political party, and say we have merged with the rival. We contested against that political party,” Kamat submitted.

When the CJI questioned the urgency, the senior counsel urged the bench to hear the matter on Wednesday or Friday, saying, “The urgency is that my functioning as a political party in Parliament has come to an absolute standstill. These MPs are not with me because the Speaker has recognised their merger with some other political party. This is intended for Parliament session.” The CJI said that he could not promise it would be listed this week. “Will see,” he added.

July 18 circular ‘unconstitutional’

On July 18, two days before the Monsoon Session in Parliament began, Birla recognised the merger of six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs—Sanjay Jadhav, Sanjay Patil, Sanjay Deshmukh, Omraje Nimbalkar, Nagesh Patil Ashtikar and Bhausaheb Wakchaure—with the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.

Sawant’s writ petition challenges “the ex-facie unconstitutional, illegal, and perverse circular dated 18.07.2026…issued by the Joint Secretary, Lok Sabha Secretariat…” recognising the merger.

Sampat said these MPs were given tickets by the Shiv Sena (UBT) and contested the Lok Sabha elections on the name and symbol belonging to party (flaming torch or mashaal). “The entire organisation, rank and file, and the leadership of the political party put immense effort and resources in campaigning for and securing their “victory…from their respective constituencies”, the petition said.



It further added that the electorate of these constituencies reposed faith in the ideology and leadership of Uddhav Thackeray. “The Lok Sabha elections in 2024 were fought, inter alia, against the candidates sponsored by Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde. The campaign, inter alia, revolved around usurpation of the legacy of Balasaheb Thackeray by Eknath Shinde through illegal means and unconstitutionally orchestrated defections. The electorate of their constituencies, in electing…accepted and validated the campaign carried out by the SS (UBT) leadership and organisation,” the petition stated.

Constitutional hara-kiri: Shiv Sena (UBT) to Supreme Court

The MPs, Sawant said in the petition, “have betrayed the faith of the electorate”, and added that their action “in defiance of their parent political party is without any constitutional or legal sanction” and “is a blatant affront to the very concept of parliamentary democracy enshrined in the Constitution which is based on the functioning of political parties”.

The plea said “the impugned circular amounts to a constitutional hara-kiri, and weakens the very foundation of our parliamentary democracy. In fact, the present case is a stark example of the prevailing constitutional crisis surrounding the functioning of political parties in Parliament and in state Legislative Assemblies.”

It urged the court to “discharge its role as the guardian of the Constitution to issue effective directions striking down the impugned circular and nullify the attempts of” the MPs “to undermine the democratic framework by functioning in the House in collusion with rival political parties.”



The petitioner said that “parliamentary democracy being a part of the basic structure of our Constitution”, it is imperative for the court “to save our democracy from the political machinations” of MPs.

World.title: Ahmedabad feels ripples of Delhi CJP protest
World.content:
Ahmedabad saw two protests organised in solidarity with Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on Monday morning. One was held at Law Garden, a tourist spot in the city beside a private university, where a few people who had gathered were taken away by police.

But nothing seemed to have prepared the authorities for the one held at 6 pm in the Ellisbridge section of Ashram Road, the city’s main commercial artery, outside the iconic MJ Library. Young people swarmed the area with placards and slogans in support of activist Sonam Wangchuk. They ran into bylanes when the police came for them.

This made the police personnel follow the protesters through the lanes and bylanes opposite Ellisbridge and Nehru Bridge. The bridges over the Sabarmati River are more than two kilometres apart.

The first lot of protesters, who had gathered to also demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, were detained around 6 pm.

As police personnel from Zone-7, which encompasses eight police stations, led by Sector-1 Joint Commissioner of Police (JCP) Niraj Kumar Badgujar, attempted to detain and send people to Vejalpur police station, the protesters began splintering into groups even as more and more people joined them later.

Civil rights activist Swati Goswami, who helped coordinate the protest, was among the first to be detained at 6:02 pm.

Speaking to The Indian Express from outside the Vejalpur police station after being released, she said: “There have been more than 22 paper leaks in Gujarat alone. Thousands of government schools have been shut down, forcing lakhs of children out of schools due to unaffordable private education. Even higher education is with the right-wing and discourages healthy discourse on human and civil rights. We demand action, accountability, reforms, answers and resignations. The youth of Gujarat will not repeat the mistakes of their older generations.”



While several protestors, both men and women, were forced into the police vehicles after two and a half hours of agitation, others went willingly and were deposited at police stations, where the slogans continued till they were set free after 9 pm.

JCP Badgujar said, “The protesters do not have police permission, and we have detained more than 150 people.”

The Indian Express witnessed the face-off between one such splinter group of about 80-odd youths and policemen stationed outside Gandhigram railway station, which is close to the Ashram Road site where the main protest was taking place.

This moving group walked into the sidelanes and clustered on the parallel road filled with offices and residences and began sloganeering as police vehicles and personnel with lathis followed them on foot.
